tests.name: workspace/name resolves to the joined path
tests.reason: Short project references must resolve only to an existing workspace/project and report its names and absolute path.

tests.name: an absolute path inside the sandbox resolves and is normalised; names are derived
tests.reason: A valid absolute project path with a trailing slash must normalize to the same canonical project identity.

tests.name: missing project, bad names and escapes are refused with codes
tests.reason: Missing directories, malformed references, lexical escapes and symlink escapes must fail with distinct PROJECT_NOT_FOUND/PATH_NOT_ALLOWED outcomes.

tests.name: a directory inside a project is refused and names the project
tests.reason: A project subdirectory cannot masquerade as a project; refusal must identify the containing project for recovery.

tests.name: directories above or outside a project are refused with PROJECT_NOT_FOUND
tests.reason: A sandbox/workspace directory or non-project folder cannot be used as a project root, even when it exists.

tests.name: loadAgents lists only chat-capable entries with models, options, accounts and defaults
tests.reason: Discovery must exclude terminal-only agents while preserving literal models/options/default account and capability data supplied by independent provider records.

tests.name: resolveModelSelection: defaults, validation, effort alias, merge with current, drop foreign options
tests.reason: Launch selection must default to the right model, normalize the effort alias/case, reject unsupported values and preserve only valid carried options.

tests.name: a model without option descriptors takes no options, as the GUI shows it no chips: any is refused; an empty catalogue refuses
tests.reason: A model with no declared options must reject any supplied option, including options-only edits; an unavailable model catalogue must refuse launch.

tests.name: validateAccountId accepts system and family accounts, refuses the rest with the valid list
tests.reason: Account selection must accept system and the selected family while rejecting cross-family IDs, preventing accidental use of another login.

tests.name: supports.goals projects the provider's goal capability into the MCP catalogue
tests.reason: The provider goals capability must reach discovery intact rather than hiding supported goal commands.

tests.name: an empty model never wins: an empty current or input model resolves like an omitted one, and its options are validated
tests.reason: Empty input/current model IDs must use a real default/current model and still validate options, preventing blank launches or invalid-option bypass.

tests.name: a model switch carries an option only when the new model advertises it and accepts the carried value
tests.reason: A model switch must drop carried options/values the new model does not accept while preserving supported values.

tests.name: a degraded provider row (an older host's) is normalised field by field, never thrown on
tests.reason: Older/malformed provider records must degrade field by field without crashing discovery or granting capabilities from truthy non-booleans.

tests.name: a model's context window reaches the view when the catalogue states a usable one
tests.reason: Only a positive numeric provider context window must reach discovery; invalid strings/negative values must not become usable limits.

tests.name: the launch default is the picker's (resolveLaunchModel): a default-flagged legacy model is never chosen, and resolveModelSelection agrees with defaultModel
tests.reason: Legacy-default models must never be selected implicitly; literal opus/haiku options and explicit legacy inclusion prove this without calling the picker for the expected answer.

tests.name: schema accepts the two shapes and rejects mixed or empty ones
tests.reason: Attachment input must accept exactly path or name/base64 variants, rejecting mixed and empty input before any upload.

tests.name: uploads a sandbox file and literal base64 bytes with the right metadata in order
tests.reason: Real file and decoded inline bytes, MIME/name metadata and input ordering must reach the host upload boundary unchanged.

tests.name: refuses more than 8, a path outside the sandbox (incl. a symlink escape), a missing file, bad base64, and oversize
tests.reason: More than eight attachments, unsafe realpaths, missing files, invalid base64 and a file over the documented image limit must refuse with the intended reason.

tests.name: attachment extensions cannot supply inherited object properties as MIME types
tests.reason: An extension such as constructor must not obtain inherited Object properties as a MIME type; ordinary extension inference still works.

tests.name: a relative path resolves against the sandbox root, as read_file's does
tests.reason: Relative attachment paths must resolve under fsRoot rather than the daemon process or caller working directory.

tests.name: a mimeType override is read as the host reads it: trimmed, lower-cased, blank meaning absent
tests.reason: Explicit MIME values must be trimmed/lowercased, blank must defer to inference and image-size checks must follow the normalized value.

tests.name: an unreadable sandbox file is the caller's error, not an internal one
tests.reason: Unreadable files must be a safe INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than exposing private filesystem errors as INTERNAL.

tests.name: nothing is uploaded when a later attachment fails validation
tests.reason: Every input must validate before the first upload, preventing orphaned host attachments when a later input is invalid.

tests.name: a path attachment sends the bytes it was validated at, even if the file grows before its upload
tests.reason: The uploaded stream must stop at its validated file length when the source grows, preventing unapproved bytes from crossing the boundary.

tests.name: an empty sandbox file uploads as an empty attachment
tests.reason: A zero-length regular file must be accepted and uploaded as zero bytes, rather than treating it as missing/invalid data.

tests.name: every file opened to validate an attachment is closed again, whatever the outcome
tests.reason: Open file descriptors must return to their initial count after accepted and rejected validation, preventing long-lived daemon descriptor exhaustion.

tests.name: a FIFO in the sandbox is refused at once, never waited on
tests.reason: A FIFO must fail immediately as a non-regular file rather than blocking the daemon waiting for a writer.

tests.name: base64 must be canonical: some data, padding only to a multiple of 4, never 4n+1 data characters
tests.reason: Base64 must be canonical (valid data/padding/length); malformed encoding must not silently produce different bytes.

tests.name: a host refusal while sending names the attachment it refused, keeping the code and the detail
tests.reason: Host rejection must retain deliberate error code/detail and identify the failed attachment index for caller recovery.

tests.name: a seam that rejects (any DaemonApi) still names the attachment: HOST_UNAVAILABLE, its cause logged and never echoed
tests.reason: A rejected upload promise must become safe HOST_UNAVAILABLE naming the attachment while keeping its private cause server-side.

tests.name: tools/list and instructions preserve audience names, MCP annotations and context byte budgets
tests.reason: MCP design §9.5 explicitly specifies serialized catalog, description and instruction byte budgets. Actual SDK tools/list and host serialization must preserve public audience keys and annotations while staying within those independent limits; no other owner measures both catalog audiences and instruction variants.

tests.name: request runs the app's own route with the caller's bearer and parses JSON
tests.reason: The real injected HTTP route must receive the calling bearer, query/body data, and return parsed JSON plus its status.

tests.name: request returns a non-JSON body as text and a 404 for unknown routes
tests.reason: Non-JSON responses must remain text and an absent route must retain HTTP404, rather than failing JSON parsing.

tests.name: subscribe receives every published EventMessage and unsubscribes cleanly
tests.reason: Actual Broadcaster delivery must reach the subscriber and stop after public unsubscribe, preventing leaked/cross-call listeners.

tests.name: a thrown upload is HOST_UNAVAILABLE, as a thrown daemon call is: the cause is logged, never returned, and the stream is released
tests.reason: Thrown host/source-stream failures must map to safe HOST_UNAVAILABLE and release unread streams; genuine upload caps remain413, preventing private paths/leaks.

tests.name: a cap refusal wrapped as another error's cause is still 413 UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE, with the refusal's own message
tests.reason: Wrapped upload-too-large errors must retain413/UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE, rather than exposing wrapper/socket messages; unrelated causes remain503.

tests.name: request appends opts.query to a path that already carries a query string
tests.reason: Query options must append to an existing path query and encode spaces/ampersands without dropping existing keys.

tests.name: the 503 upload answer (no agent chat service) releases the stream it will never read
tests.reason: When chat service is unavailable, a refused unread upload stream must be destroyed instead of leaking its source.

tests.name: a path attachment the seam refuses, or that fails mid-read, leaves no file open
tests.reason: Real attachment file descriptors must close after an unavailable service or failure after the first stream chunk.

tests.name: a throwing subscriber stays subscribed and cannot block delivery to other callers
tests.reason: A subscriber exception must neither unregister it nor prevent another subscriber receiving current and later events.

tests.name: visual pages answer outcomes: the publisher's and preview's messages pass, a store failure's cause and anything unexpected never do
tests.reason: Public render/preview outcomes and deliberate failure codes must pass through, while storage/unexpected private error causes stay out of responses.

tests.name: listDirectory / readFileRange read through FsTools under the LIVE fsRoot, inside the sandbox only; withPrincipal forwards them
tests.reason: Filesystem operations through the principal-bound real API must follow the live sandbox root after configuration changes and reject paths outside it.

tests.name: daemonError reads the chat envelope, the flat shape and a bare string
tests.reason: Daemon error transport must normalize nested/flat legacy envelopes and non-JSON failures while retaining deliberate code/message/detail.

tests.name: a 5xx without a deliberate code never echoes the body (spec §4.5)
tests.reason: Undeliberate5xx bodies and errno codes must never reveal host paths; only a route-owned deliberate failure may expose its safe message.

tests.name: a 4xx whose body names nothing falls back to the status table and never echoes the body
tests.reason: Code-less4xx responses must use stable status-derived codes and avoid echoing arbitrary HTML/body data.

tests.name: a code-less 4xx with an empty message falls back to the status text, never to an empty message
tests.reason: A blank code-less4xx message must still produce a nonempty useful error from status text/fallback; a valid supplied message wins.

tests.name: strict parse per audience: each audience's only-inputs are stripped from the other's schema and refused
tests.reason: Actual execution must reject audience-only/unknown fields and preserve permitted inputs/defaults; removed private shape inventory added no protection.

tests.name: TOOL_NOT_FOUND for another audience's tool or an unknown name; a tool of any group runs for any chat (no switch)
tests.reason: Unknown/other-audience tools must refuse before any run with a bounded name; groups must not require an obsolete enable switch.

tests.name: Admin from a workflow-owned chat is ADMIN_NOT_AVAILABLE at once: no preview, no card, no run
tests.reason: Workflow-owned callers must never preview, approve or execute Admin operations, even if an approval port is present.

tests.name: an Admin card: what runs is the frozen copy that was shown; pins and the approval reach run; grant options follow the mode
tests.reason: Only the approved argument values and preview pins may run; approved pins, reason and grant eligibility must reach the effect without depending on Object.freeze. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: card outcomes: denied quotes the user, timed out, cancelled; no port fails closed; an oversized preview never opens a card
tests.reason: Denied/timed-out/cancelled/missing-port outcomes must prevent effects, and an unshowable preview must fail before requesting approval.

tests.name: grants: honoured for a full-access caller without a card; never below full-access
tests.reason: Stored grants may bypass a card only for Full access; the same grant must not authorize a narrowed caller.

tests.name: a chosen grant is committed only after the re-gate passes; refused there, or not recordable, the row claims no grant
tests.reason: Grant persistence must occur only after refreshing/re-gating the caller; declined/unrecordable grants must not be claimed on the result row.

tests.name: an approved workflow create records the new workflow only in the grant its outcome names
tests.reason: A created workflow may join only the exact grant authorized by the approval outcome; unrelated chat grants must remain unchanged.

tests.name: boundary cards: cross-workspace Act names its one target and git identity; same-workspace Act below full-access cards without grants
tests.reason: Cross-workspace boundary approval must identify its exact target/git identity; same-workspace approval below Full access must offer no grant. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: turn policy and the exchange: hop + 1, a new exchange at hop 1, EXCHANGE_LIMIT past 8, never into a broader chat, plan carries on
tests.reason: Caused turns must inherit planning, increment/start exchanges, refuse hop9 and reject broader target modes before effects.

tests.name: a session the call creates takes the exchange but no mode check
tests.reason: A newly created chat must receive exchange provenance although no pre-existing target head can be read.

tests.name: every daemon request carries the caller's principal, forced: a tool cannot name another; agent projectPath is canonical or ""
tests.reason: The executor must force every backend request to the true caller principal and canonical project, overriding a forged principal supplied by a tool.

tests.name: results: a record is ok()-wrapped, a CallToolResult passes through, an unexpected throw is INTERNAL without its text; an aborted call is cancelled
tests.reason: Results must preserve valid MCP content, wrap data, hide unexpected error causes and cancel aborted calls rather than executing them.

tests.name: every gated outcome carries the row's reference: granted (with the grant's scope), timed out, cancelled
tests.reason: Every approved/granted/timed-out/cancelled operation must retain its real approval reference/scope for the user-visible audit row.

tests.name: tier(args, scope): the tier and family the scope resolved drive the gate, the card and grants — fail closed without one
tests.reason: Argument/scope-dependent tier and family must control gating; absent family data must fail closed rather than permit unapproved writes.

tests.name: Admin cards: the computed adminFamily is the card's; a preview may only make it stricter (a strict subset of its grant scopes)
tests.reason: A preview may restrict grant scopes only; it cannot widen computed Admin authorization or change the operation family.

tests.name: a tier or adminFamily function that throws: the call is an error and run is never called
tests.reason: Failure while computing tier/family must prevent the effect and become an error, rather than accidentally defaulting to a safe tier.

tests.name: a caller with no canonical project of its own is never offered a grant (findGrant would never honour it)
tests.reason: A caller whose project no longer resolves cannot receive an unusable/misleading grant for that project.

tests.name: a cancelled card says why: a restart withdraws it (call again later), a closed chat ends it
tests.reason: Restart/closed-chat cancellation must explain the recoverable state and execute nothing; generic wording-only repetition was removed.

tests.name: the card carries what the port re-checks: pending temp projects and a workflow-referenced prompt
tests.reason: Approval facts must include pending temp-project targets and workflow-referenced prompt identity so the port can recheck real authorization.

tests.name: a grant is re-checked on the refreshed caller: no longer full-access → refused, nothing runs
tests.reason: A grant found before refresh must be rejected if the caller loses Full access before execution, preventing a time-of-check authorization bypass.

tests.name: listFiles accepts relative and absolute paths and returns sorted file, dir, and symlink entries
tests.reason: Relative/absolute sandbox directory reads must return the same sorted files/directories/symlinks and literal byte sizes.

tests.name: listFiles rejects sandbox escapes and missing directories with safe errors
tests.reason: Direct and symlink directory escapes must refuse without exposing paths; missing directories must give a safe caller error.

tests.name: listFiles caps entries and marks truncated after 500
tests.reason: A501-entry real directory must return500 entries, sorted and flagged truncated, preserving the documented listing ceiling.

tests.name: readFileWindow reads the default window and supports byte-offset paging
tests.reason: The default file window must read65536 bytes and resume at its byte offset to return the uncut tail.

tests.name: readFileWindow refuses binary files, directories, and missing files with safe ToolErrors
tests.reason: Binary/missing files must give safe errors, and a directory must be distinguishable so the public tool can list it.

tests.name: readFileWindow blocks symlinks that resolve outside the sandbox
tests.reason: A file symlink escaping fsRoot must refuse before its target bytes can be read.

tests.name: readFileWindow ends a window on a UTF-8 character boundary and says how many bytes it consumed
tests.reason: Mixed1/2/3/4-byte characters must page without replacement, gaps or overlap; consumed bytes/truncation must let the caller reconstruct the source. Eight alignment cycles retain all edge classes.

tests.name: readFileWindow: a window narrower than its first character takes that character whole, so paging never stalls
tests.reason: A maxBytes smaller than one codepoint must take that whole character and advance, rather than hang pagination.

tests.name: the §5.2 matrix: reads and acts by target class and permission mode
tests.reason: The independently written permission/access/target matrix must yield the correct allow/card decision for each documented mode.

tests.name: Admin: a card in EVERY permission mode, cross-project marked, never while planning, never for a workflow-owned chat
tests.reason: Admin effects must always require a correctly scoped card, never run for planning/workflow-owned callers and never fabricate a family.

tests.name: workflow-owned callers: every card becomes a denial; cross-project Act is denied in every mode; own-project work is allowed
tests.reason: Workflow-owned callers must deny cross-project effects/cards while retaining permitted local work and Full-access reads.

tests.name: plan mode: reads allowed; turn-causing Act carries on; data-changing Act refused unless planSafe
tests.reason: Planning must preserve reads and caused planning turns while blocking edits except explicitly plan-safe operations.

tests.name: paths outside a project, self targets and not-own children are refused before anything else
tests.reason: Outside paths, forbidden self targets and unrelated children must be denied even before Admin approval can be requested.

tests.name: cards: Act covers what it reads; the wider boundary names a read card; a grantable cross-project card names its one target
tests.reason: Mixed read/write scope must choose the strongest boundary and offer a grant only for exactly one eligible target.

tests.name: an unknown permission mode is the narrowest: every boundary cards
tests.reason: Unknown future runtime modes must be treated as narrowest instead of accidentally inheriting broader access.

tests.name: workspace-level targets (S13): own workspace = own row; another workspace = the other-workspace row (cards below Full access, Act always a card, never grantable)
tests.reason: Workspace-wide scopes must obey their own/other-workspace matrix, never receive project grants and remain unavailable for workflow-owned writes.

tests.name: an unknown project (a stored path that is no project now): a boundary card in every mode, never a grant target; Admin cross-project; workflow-owned refused
tests.reason: Deleted/unresolvable stored project identities must always card, never become a grant target or bypass workflow-owned restrictions.

tests.name: paths: inside a project (symlinks resolved) → that project; the root, a workspace, outside the sandbox → outside
tests.reason: Path classification must use symlink targets/canonical projects, treating sandbox/workspace/non-project/outside paths as outside.

tests.name: paths: a file beside the projects is no project — workspace level, root level, or linked to; a real project's files are
tests.reason: Files beside projects, including links to them, must never be classified as a project and thereby gain project-scoped access.

tests.name: workspace-level targets: the caller's own workspace is own, any other (and every one for a caller with no project) is other-workspace
tests.reason: Workspace scope claims must deduplicate and classify against the caller canonical workspace; unbound callers must fail closed.

tests.name: target classes, and a caller bound to no project: every target is other
tests.reason: Project/path/pending-project facts must classify own/sibling/other scopes and report denied paths, including callers with no project.

tests.name: own children: lineage parent = the caller AND agentCreated; a GUI fork is never the agent's
tests.reason: Child-only authorization must require both correct parent and agentCreated; self uses its own policy while GUI/unrelated/missing children are refused through real gateFacts.

tests.name: workflow-owned: owner on the tab or any ancestor; a closed ancestor fails closed only behind an agent-made link
tests.reason: Workflow ownership must propagate through live ancestors and fail closed for lost agent-made parents/cycles, without treating ordinary GUI orphans as owned.

tests.name: workflow-owned: the inheritable lineage marker is proof on its own — even behind a GUI fork of a closed parent
tests.reason: The persisted workflowOwned lineage marker must retain restrictions behind a closed parent and propagate through descendants.

tests.name: (a) a target broader than the caller is refused; the same or narrower is not
tests.reason: Every literal documented permission-mode pair must reject privilege escalation and accept equal/narrower targets; expected order is no longer imported from production.

tests.name: (a) a thread the caller opens runs in its mode by default, or a narrower one named; a broader one is refused
tests.reason: Opened-chat defaults and explicit choices must never exceed the caller breadth, and advertised allowed modes must match the literal independent policy order.

tests.name: (a) an unknown mode fails closed: a caller's is the narrowest (reaches nothing, opens nothing broader), a target's the broadest
tests.reason: Unknown caller modes must reach no known target/open choice and default only to Supervised; unknown target modes must always refuse.

tests.name: paging back by olderTurns through the tool never skips a turn, however much each read sheds
tests.reason: Real durable history, index and MCP pagination must reconstruct every older turn without gaps despite result shedding; unit cursor stubs cannot prove this chain.

tests.name: a turn larger than five pages: its latest rows are returned, and the hint names the call for the turns before it
tests.reason: An actual turn spanning more than five host pages must expose recent rows and an actionable cursor for earlier turns, rather than claiming completeness.

tests.name: restarted onto a fresh index: the turns the window no longer holds are named until the catch-up, then read whole
tests.reason: After rebuilding a fresh index, evicted turns must be reported unavailable until actual catch-up makes their durable rows readable.

tests.name: no page is read when the window already holds the range, when the host predates history, or when nothing is older
tests.reason: Available-window/older-host/no-older-history responses must remain complete without reporting invented unavailable ranges or making unnecessary host history calls.

tests.name: a host repeating its history cursor is bounded to five pages and reports missing turns
tests.reason: A repeating host cursor must stop at five pages and explicitly name the unread turn range, preventing infinite history walks.

tests.name: a page read that fails — 503 INDEX_UNAVAILABLE, another status, a throw, a body that is no page — is never an error: the window's rows are served and the turns left are named
tests.reason: Unavailable/rejected/malformed history pages must preserve readable window data while reporting exactly what was not read.

tests.name: a page's rows without the fields the transcript reads are dropped, never read into a failed call; bounds that are not the host's read nothing
tests.reason: Malformed rows/cursors/bounds must not enter transcript parsing or cause a whole read to fail; valid rows remain usable.

tests.name: a host without a usable index: the range's turns with no row in the window are named, and nothing is read
tests.reason: A host without a usable index must name the requested turns absent from its retained window instead of silently presenting partial data as complete.

tests.name: an index that has not caught up with the thread — it knows fewer turns — cannot place the window: the turns up to the window's oldest are named, and nothing is read
tests.reason: An index that has not caught up must not treat hasOlder:false as proof that no earlier history exists.

tests.name: where the window begins is its oldest activity row that retention would drop — not a row it keeps whatever its age — and a turnless one is placed by its time
tests.reason: Retention boundary must come from an evictable oldest row, with turnless rows placed by timestamps; permanently retained work cannot create false gaps.

tests.name: a drill-in while the index catches up is judged by the subagent's own oldest row left, from the turn it was launched in
tests.reason: Subagent drill-in missing ranges must use that agent rows and launch turn while the index catches up, rather than the parent retention boundary.

tests.name: a drill-in on a host without a usable index names the subagent's own span, as while the index catches up: a parent's row is no row of the subagent's
tests.reason: Without a usable index, a parent row cannot prove a subagent turn complete; the agent own span must be reported unavailable.

tests.name: an agent with no row left ends its span at its end when its last task row is Claude's end — an end not stamped with the agent's own id — else at the oldest row any agent kept
tests.reason: A lost subagent window must end at its actual task completion (even a Claude completion unstamped with agent ID), otherwise at the correct retained boundary.

tests.name: the opening row of work still running says nothing about where the parent's window begins: the fold keeps it whatever its age
tests.reason: A permanently kept running-work opening cannot shift the parent missing-history boundary backward.

tests.name: the opening row of work still running says nothing about where a drill-in's rows begin, nor where the rows every agent kept do
tests.reason: A kept running opening cannot shift drill-in or other-agent retention boundaries either; each missing span must use evictable activity.

tests.name: an empty page with a null cursor at the window's boundary or at a host's cursor — what a host answers where it could not plan a block or read one back whole — is a failed read in both views, never the thread's first turn reached
tests.reason: An empty null-cursor host page must report failed recovery at real history/window boundaries, rather than falsely claiming the first turn was reached.

tests.name: the first page below turn end + 1 — the one cursor the walk mints itself — may come back empty: with no activity below it, the thread's start is reached, and the parent view names only the turns with no row at all
tests.reason: The first synthetic turn-end cursor may legitimately return no activity; empty resumed chat-only turns must not be reported as unreadable history.

tests.name: a drill-in's failed read starts at the turn the subagent was launched in, as its span without an index does: it has no rows before it
tests.reason: A failed drill-in walk must never report turns before the subagent launch.

tests.name: a drill-in's page-limit span starts at the turn the subagent was launched in too, and both forms of the limit's hint name the call that reads just those turns
tests.reason: Five-page drill-in limits must respect the launch turn and supply the next exact public read call for both hint forms.

tests.name: the parent view's net: after a walk, a turn of the range with no row in the merged snapshot is still named — beside a failed read's turns, never past the page limit; a drill-in has none
tests.reason: The parent missing-row net must combine failed-read spans without reporting turns past a page-limit boundary or inventing a drill-in net.

tests.name: repeated history rows keep the window values once, in time order, with current checkpoints
tests.reason: Merged repeated history rows must deduplicate in chronological order while preserving fresher window values/checkpoints.

tests.name: tokens: ≥ 128 bits of base64url, distinct, single use, released by the minter, expired after the TTL
tests.reason: Opaque tokens must provide128bits, be unique/base64url, single-use/releasable and expire at30000ms. Platform Date.now mocking removes a production injection hook; fixed16/30000 oracles protect the documented constants.

tests.name: a minted principal is a copy: changing the minter's object changes nothing a route reads
tests.reason: Mutating a minter-owned principal object after minting must not forge the identity resolved by a route.

tests.name: the hook: no header is the user; a live token is its principal and the header never reaches the route; a bad token is 401, never the user
tests.reason: The real Fastify hook must default no header to user, consume/remove a valid token and reject invalid/reused tokens401 rather than downgrade them.

tests.name: InjectDaemonApi forwards agent and external principals without changing plain user calls
tests.reason: In-process DaemonApi requests must resolve the agent/external caller principal and leave ordinary user requests unchanged. Actual Fastify hook observations protect authority identity through request minting/release, beyond pure token validation.

tests.name: the external credential id names the identity, never the secret, and is stable
tests.reason: An external credential ID must be stable per identity, different for another identity and expose neither username nor bearer-secret material.

tests.name: both apps resolve principals: the socket app and the HTTP app (behind its bearer); a bad token is 401 on each
tests.reason: Both real server transports must install principal handling and reject bad tokens behind HTTP bearer auth; testing the bare hook alone cannot prove installation.

tests.name: the external /mcp acts as external {credentialId} on every daemon call; the /mcp request itself and a direct REST call are the user's
tests.reason: Actual external /mcp backend calls must act as credential-scoped external principals, while HTTP MCP/direct REST requests remain user principals.

tests.name: through createServer's real routes: the remote app strips trusted turn, merge-back and interrupt fields; the socket app keeps them
tests.reason: Trusted causedBy, interrupt cause and cascade fields must survive socket control but be stripped by real remote turn/merge/interrupt routes. Literal forwarded request bodies independently verify the transport trust boundary; helper-only API tests cannot prove route wiring.

tests.name: sendCommand retries HOST_UNAVAILABLE with the SAME commandId up to 3 times, then throws; other errors are final
tests.reason: Transient host-unavailable retries must reuse one commandId and stop at documented attempts; other errors must not replay side effects.

tests.name: a thrown daemon call surfaces HOST_UNAVAILABLE without its private path
tests.reason: A thrown socket/backend failure must become safe HOST_UNAVAILABLE without its private path after bounded retries.

tests.name: readThread refuses any answer that is not a snapshot as INTERNAL, an empty one included
tests.reason: Thread reads expecting a snapshot must reject event/null bodies as INTERNAL, preventing downstream misinterpretation of a successful wrong envelope.

tests.name: oversized MCP results remain byte-bounded, flagged and valid UTF-8
tests.reason: Oversized ASCII/multibyte JSON results must fit60000 UTF8 bytes, mark truncation and preserve valid character boundaries.

tests.name: the MCP result cap accepts exactly 60000 bytes and flags one byte over
tests.reason: Exactly60000 serialized bytes must remain whole and60001 must truncate, protecting the inclusive public result limit.

tests.name: ToolError surfaces code and message; sandbox errors never echo the path; unknown errors are generic
tests.reason: Deliberate ToolError code/detail must survive while sandbox paths/unexpected internal error messages stay private.

tests.name: TodoError maps its status to a code and keeps its (safe) message
tests.reason: Public todo-client errors must map404/400/409 to stable tool error codes rather than INTERNAL.

tests.name: an error message is capped whatever it echoes: at most 4_000 code points, a cut one ending in …
tests.reason: Reflected error strings must fit4000 codepoints with a visible cut; short deliberate messages/details must stay unchanged.

tests.name: same workspace: Full access opens it at once; below Full access the user approves or denies a boundary card with no grant
tests.reason: Real socket caller derivation, approval routes and session persistence must enforce sibling-project mode boundaries, denial no-effects and unoffered-grant refusal. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: another workspace: a card in every mode naming both git identities; Full access may grant it for this chat and that one project only, honoured only while Full access
tests.reason: Real cross-workspace grants must persist exact chat/target identity, authorize only that pair, stop applying when mode narrows and disappear on user revocation.

tests.name: another workspace below Full access: every mode cards with no grant; a planning chat's caused turn plans; a workflow-owned chat is refused without a card
tests.reason: Real transport policy must propagate planning while rejecting unsupported-plan agents and workflow-owned cross-project effects before opening tabs.

tests.name: external callers: address validation only — any project, no card, Full access by default; chat-only fields refused
tests.reason: Authenticated external MCP must be full trust without cards/lineage while rejecting chat-only or invalid project args at the wire.

tests.name: other-workspace metadata cards below Full access; same-workspace metadata is free and content needs Auto; list_projects only counts other workspaces
tests.reason: Real metadata/content/search transport gating must hide inaccessible workspace data and return authorized content after actual user approval.

tests.name: advertised to a fresh chat → Admin card (no grant even at Full access) → SKILL.md equals the card; Supervised cards too; planning and workflow-owned refused; external writes without a card
tests.reason: Native SKILL.md persistence must equal the approved card bytes; deny/planning/workflow restrictions and non-grantability must survive real route/store wiring. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: create global + project prompts (no card, stamped as the agent's, unpinnable); edit the agent's (no card) vs the user's (card, grantable at Full access); a workflow-referenced one cards as workflows, never grantable
tests.reason: Real prompt ownership, pin security and persisted grants must distinguish own/user/workflow-used prompts through public transports and stores.

tests.name: createdBy is named only for the caller itself and chats of its workspace; another workspace's, or an unknown thread, reads as its kind
tests.reason: Real prompt rows and update results must suppress cross-workspace/closed creator identities while retaining permitted creator data.

tests.name: a repository prompt whose only checkout was deleted: the create card shows its body in full and pins it, never as missing
tests.reason: A repository prompt must remain addressable by id and visible on workflow cards after its last checkout is deleted; actual git repository/store lookup is required.

tests.name: the grant made on the create card covers every later call in that chat; a user-made sub-workflow it does not cover forces a card
tests.reason: One persisted workflow grant must support the full shell failure/debug/fix/re-run/delete lifecycle while a newly referenced ungranted child forces fresh approval. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: set_workflow_secret: an Admin card in a chat holding a workflows grant, no grant option, the value only in the store — never in results, events, cards or files
tests.reason: Typed workflow secrets must reach the real store/executed shell but never results/events/card/journal/config, even under a workflow grant.

tests.name: a workflow whose project is in another workspace: a card naming that workspace's identity, never a grant
tests.reason: Cross-workspace workflow creation must show the target identity, persist only after approval and offer/record no grant.

tests.name: session cost: Claude estimated (1h cache writes, the picker's resolved model), Codex estimated, Grok reported; floor flags; weekly buckets from the scanner; quota without emails for chats
tests.reason: Actual token scanner, chat usage and tool transports must yield literal per-session/week cost/calendar results and floor flags; chat quota must hide emails.

tests.name: two notify round trips and a wait, Codex's own send refused, WAIT_CYCLE once raised, EXCHANGE_LIMIT at hop 8, a user turn starts a fresh exchange
tests.reason: Real reply router/lineage queue/transport wiring must deliver notify exactly once, return wait answers, enforce modes/cycles/hops and reset exchange on a user turn.

tests.name: workflow-owned: no Admin tool or request_toolset advertised; Admin calls ADMIN_NOT_AVAILABLE, every card a denial — inherited by the chats it opens, even after it closes
tests.reason: Real per-chat manifests and actual operations must deny Admin for workflow-owned lineage, including descendants after parent closure, while allowing local Act.

tests.name: planning: data-changing Act and Admin refused; a turn it causes elsewhere plans too, and an agent without plan mode is refused
tests.reason: Planning caller derivation must block real persisted mutations and propagate plan to other threads while refusing agents unable to plan.

tests.name: detected in each CLI's user config and a project's config, denied in the chat manifest, and applied by each provider's launch: Claude disallowedTools, Codex enabled=false, Grok shadowed, OpenCode deny rules
tests.reason: Real native user/project MCP configs must be detected and denied in provider launch payloads without leaking bearers; actual card rejects unsafe config changes.

tests.name: respond_to_request cannot reach it, the card route refuses agent and external principals, two answers race to one winner
tests.reason: Actual card endpoints must be user-only, reject agent/external principals, resolve concurrent answers once and cancel when the owner chat closes.

tests.name: an external and an in-chat create launch with a profile named by name (unattended), the reads report it, an unknown or unprepared one fails — never Global
tests.reason: Real profile store/name resolution/read projections must launch unattended with the selected profile and refuse missing/unprepared profiles without silently opening Global.

tests.name: a workflow agent block names a profile; validation flags a missing one; deleting a used profile is refused until the user confirms the workflows that use it
tests.reason: Real workflow validation and profile-delete preconditions must retain referenced profiles until current workflow uses are explicitly confirmed.

tests.name: tools/list pins every tool's required params and annotations (spec §12 snapshot)
tests.reason: Literal external tool names/required JSON params/MCP annotations and closed input schemas must survive actual tools/list serialization.

tests.name: tools/list is generated from the catalog's external audience: each entry's _meta names its chat tier and toolset
tests.reason: Actual external wire metadata must expose tier/toolset values clients use, including dynamic Admin tools, independent of internal catalog declarations.

tests.name: a tool call returns structuredContent + text; a ToolError becomes isError with a code; the api is built with the caller's bearer
tests.reason: Real tools/call responses must contain both text/structured data, deliberate tool error codes and the authenticated request bearer on backend calls.

tests.name: each tool's zod defaults apply before run(): list_sessions {} answers with kind all, attention off
tests.reason: Defaults must be applied before execution; empty list_sessions args must include both chat and terminal tabs.

tests.name: arguments a tool's schema refuses answer the §4.5 envelope: isError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, one line naming the fields
tests.reason: Schema refusals must use the documented INVALID_ARGUMENT envelope and identify fields before any tool effect.

tests.name: an argument name the tool does not take is refused and named, never dropped: a misspelled optional argument cannot take its default
tests.reason: Misspelled optional fields must be rejected rather than silently dropped and replaced with defaults.

tests.name: over the wire, a 2 MiB enum value is refused in a short INVALID_ARGUMENT, not a 2 MiB one
tests.reason: A2MiB invalid enum value must yield a short useful error instead of reflecting megabytes into the client.

tests.name: a call without an arguments object is a call with none: the defaults apply
tests.reason: Omitted arguments must behave as an empty argument object, preserving documented tool defaults.

tests.name: an unknown tool's name is quoted capped: a 2 MiB name gets a short −32602, not a 2 MiB one
tests.reason: A2MiB unknown tool name must produce a bounded JSONRPC -32602 refusal, preventing output amplification.

tests.name: the route takes a 2 MiB tools/call — its own 16 MiB body limit, past Fastify's 1 MiB default
tests.reason: The MCP route must accept bodies larger than Fastify default1MiB up to its own16MiB contract.

tests.name: a client that disconnects aborts the request's signal: a wait lets go of the bus at once, not at its timeout
tests.reason: A disconnected client must cancel actual waits and release bus resources immediately rather than wait for the tool timeout.

tests.name: a client already gone when the route runs gets nothing done for it: its 'close' has fired and will not fire again
tests.reason: A request already disconnected at handler entry must perform no tool effect because no later close event will arrive.

tests.name: GET and DELETE /mcp answer 405 with Allow: POST
tests.reason: Unsupported HTTP GET/DELETE methods must return405 with Allow:POST.

tests.name: POST /mcp answers 406 unless Accept lists both application/json and text/event-stream
tests.reason: Streamable HTTP must require both JSON and event-stream Accept types, returning406 otherwise.

tests.name: the daemon mounts /mcp on the HTTP transport behind the bearer hook, and every tool's daemon call carries the caller's bearer
tests.reason: Real createServer HTTP mounting must require daemon auth and forward its bearer to all backend calls.

tests.name: the unix-socket transport never serves /mcp
tests.reason: The trusted Unix socket must never mount the full-trust external /mcp endpoint.

tests.name: invalid names and missing directories reject as PROJECT_NOT_FOUND before creating todos
tests.reason: Missing/traversal workspace/project names must return PROJECT_NOT_FOUND without persisting a list, including the existing sibling escape directory. Detects helper resolving a path outside the intended workspace; executor argument-shape checks do not cover these concrete raw helper names.

tests.name: a write names the list's own scope: an id from another scope is NOT_FOUND and nothing changes
tests.reason: An id from a project scope cannot be updated, deleted or toggled as a workspace id; correct scope can delete it. Literal stored name and NOT_FOUND outcome catch cross-scope writes even when id exists. General gate tests cannot protect route selection/scope ownership.

tests.name: toggleItem by 1-based index flips and explicitly sets while preserving non-task lines
tests.reason: Removed duplicate real-server facade scenario. Stable full-executor todo lifecycle now proves 1-based task indexing, flip/explicit unchecked state and byte preservation across prose, list marker and whitespace. Fails unique-protection bar; no distinct facade branch remains.

tests.name: toggleItem by text is exact after trim and case-insensitive
tests.reason: Removed duplicate facade scenario. Surviving full-executor lifecycle looks up stored Ship with leading/trailing spaces through lowercase ship and verifies the exact edited body. Fails unique-protection bar after the fixture consolidation.

tests.name: toggleItem explicit same-state set preserves the existing body
tests.reason: Removed duplicate facade same-state scenario. Surviving lifecycle verifies that setting lowercase build true preserves its existing uppercase X byte; the retained large-list owner separately verifies no update event/timestamp change. Fails unique-protection bar.

tests.name: toggleItem errors are safe and actionable
tests.reason: Empty, missing-text, ambiguous-text and absent-id requests must return the documented actionable INVALID_ARGUMENT/NOT_FOUND distinctions without succeeding. Literal task names make wrong or missing suggestions observable; ordinary success and HTTP status tests do not protect selection-error mapping.

tests.name: a missing list's id is echoed capped and escaped: one short line whatever the caller sent
tests.reason: A hostile missing list id is quoted once on one line, escaped and clipped to the documented 100-code-point caller quote bound. Detects log/error injection or oversized errors from an id, separate from task-body selector failure.

tests.name: the routes' other refusals map as the store's always did: 409 CONFLICT, 4xx INVALID_ARGUMENT, a 5xx never echoed
tests.reason: Backend 409 maps to CONFLICT, safe 4xx to INVALID_ARGUMENT, and 5xx host path is never echoed; route body selects the toggle endpoint. Fake backend supplies independent HTTP responses, while actual error mapping/serialization remain production code. Real routes cannot readily generate native failures deterministically.

tests.name: a refusal quotes the caller's item capped and escaped, and a long list's items bounded, never the whole list
tests.reason: Preserve documented 100-code-point quoted/escaped caller input, ambiguity and bounded suggestions. Use 101 characters instead of half a MiB to cross the exact echo boundary. Remove the repeated 3,000-short-item execution: the retained long-item refusal owner already verifies list total, truncation and whole error budget.

tests.name: the longest refusal there can be ends whole under the error cap, whatever the input: the quote escaped at its longest, 40 items at their cap
tests.reason: Retain real-route capped errors for control characters and lone surrogates, original item count, and unmodified <=4,000-code-point handoff. Eighty long tasks exceed the documented 40-suggestion boundary and recreate the historical oversized-suggestion failure; 3,000 tasks add disk/JSON work without another bound. Oracle remains literal escaped strings and independently counted message code points.

tests.name: a toggle is atomic: an edit landing after the tool read the list survives, and concurrent toggles both land
tests.reason: A user edit arriving after scope read and two concurrent toggles must all survive in stored markdown. Deterministic injected interleaving preserves real routes/store; literal final body catches the historical read-then-PUT lost-update bug that generic store persistence concurrency misses.

tests.name: the toggle route refuses a bad body (400) and an unknown list (404) with the todo envelope
tests.reason: Direct HTTP toggle endpoint must return 400/TODO_ERROR for malformed JSON fields and 404 for missing ids. Stable wire response is the oracle; executor field checks cannot protect another HTTP client bypassing the catalog.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {}: every CLI's summary; mode arguments without agent are refused
tests.reason: Overview must map all daemon CLI summaries and reject incompatible mode arguments; catches silently reading the wrong scope/shape.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent}: filters by kind and case-insensitive source while preserving ownership and revision
tests.reason: List filters must honor kind/case-insensitive source, retain ownership/action permissions/revisions and report installed state; catches edits aimed at managed/plugin items or hidden list matches.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent}: oversized lists preserve a prefix and report omitted rows within the byte cap
tests.reason: Oversized lists must retain the original prefix, total matched/omitted and stay under documented 60k UTF8 JSON cap; catches transport-drop or missing identity rows.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent, itemId}: hostile env and header entries expose keys only
tests.reason: Even hostile route replies carrying env/header values must expose keys only; catches actual secret disclosure from a newer or buggy backend.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent, itemId}: URL credentials are redacted but retained for an update that names no url
tests.reason: Read views must redact URL userinfo before clipping/meta mapping while omitted-url updates retain original daemon URL; catches credential leakage or credential destruction during unrelated update.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent, itemId}: a long skill body is a Unicode-safe prefix marked as incomplete
tests.reason: Whole skill document result must preserve small content/files, safely clip Unicode large content and mark incomplete; catches corrupt previews returned as full editable documents.

tests.name: get_agent_profile {agent, instructions}: Unicode pages reassemble; {agent, marketplace} lists plugins
tests.reason: Instruction pages must make forward progress/reassemble full Unicode and reject past-end offsets; marketplace mode maps plugin list separately.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile: ambiguous, unsupported and malformed batches fail before any daemon request
tests.reason: Malformed/ambiguous/unsupported batches must reject before any daemon request; catches unintended writes from misspelled or mutually incompatible action arguments.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile create: compact arguments become daemon drafts and only changed items are returned
tests.reason: Compact create arguments must map stdio/http secrets, conflict mode and documents/plugins into daemon drafts; only changed IDs may return and no raw snapshot secret may escape. Remove incidental hook create whose body/result is never checked.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile update: keep, replace, remove and add secrets without resolving their values
tests.reason: MCP update must keep unnamed secret keys daemon-side, replace/remove named values, reject incompatible transports and drop old transport fields; catches credential loss/leakage or unusable server config.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile update: an external stale revision is sent as given; conflicts carry a fresh item, confirmed absence or the original refusal
tests.reason: External explicit stale revisions must reach daemon unchanged; conflict reply must distinguish fresh item, confirmed gone and unavailable reread, without secret data; catches lost update protection or false deletion claims.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile update: partial document and hook edits preserve omitted fields and reject a wrong kind
tests.reason: Partial document/hook edits must preserve omitted body/command/event, represent removal and refuse wrong item kind; catches destructive sparse updates.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile enable/disable/delete/trust_hook/copy: current or explicit revisions, absent targets refused
tests.reason: Enable/disable/delete/trust/copy must send correct revision/target/onConflict, return correct affected identity and refuse missing/uninstalled targets; catches mutation of wrong config/native hook trust.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile write_instructions and imports: whole-text writes, revision guards, private URLs, picks
tests.reason: Instruction writes must replace whole text with revision (empty revision preserved), enrich conflict info; import scan/pick maps raw request/selection and strips private URL from result; catches truncated overwrites or wrong imported items.

tests.name: edit_agent_profile: a batch runs in order and stops at the first failure, naming what was done
tests.reason: Batch must stop after first failure and report exact completed/failed actions; catches later unintended writes and callers misreporting partial success.

tests.name: chat: a skill is added after a card showing its whole SKILL.md; never grantable; the result reports the approval
tests.reason: Chat create must show whole SKILL.md and global blast radius, remain ungrantable, write only after approval and return approval outcome; catches hidden code installation or grant bypass. Whole title prose is incidental; file content/path bytes remain contractual. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat: batch validation runs before any card or read; a stale revision is refused before the card
tests.reason: Chat validation/stale revision/missing item must refuse before card/write/read when possible; catches invalid approval prompts and accidental global mutation.

tests.name: chat: {ask: true} values are card fields; the value goes from the card to the write and never back to the agent
tests.reason: Card-typed ask value must flow only from secret field to write, absent from result/card/check request; catches routing user credential through agent or preapproval check.

tests.name: chat: every value the agent wrote is shown in full — code-loading env, secret-looking tokens — only card-typed values are hidden
tests.reason: Surviving actual approval-card owner now proves key-name/prefix/bearer/entropy warning states and safe environment references, alongside actual visible values/card-typed secret privacy; removed the test-only heuristic export.

tests.name: chat: a header bearer the agent wrote is shown as written; a server pointing at this daemon is flagged in red
tests.reason: Bearer/header/URL written by agent must display whole, flagged when daemon identifies own endpoint, with exact daemon-check input; catches approving access to Orquester without informed warning.

tests.name: chat: an update's daemon-pointing check names the item so the daemon checks its current secret values too
tests.reason: Update daemon check must name existing item to include host-only secret values, while previews show unchanged values hidden and writes use keep; catches unsafe existing bearer bypass or leaking credentials.

tests.name: chat previews are complete per item kind: a copied skill as the target gets it, executables and binaries flagged with hashes
tests.reason: Copied skill preview must use target-converted tree and expose full text, hashes/executable/binary flags and symlink warning; catches approving different code than target receives. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat previews: a plugin's provides with hook commands and MCP command lines, its files and the marketplace commit
tests.reason: Plugin preview must show provided hooks/MCP command lines, code/files and pinned commit; changed commit must block install, remote code must warn, incomplete source must refuse; distinct package supply-chain contracts. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat previews: import picks in full with the commit; a checkout that changed after the card is PREVIEW_STALE
tests.reason: Import card must include picked content/commit only, then reject changed file digest before write; import scan must require card before egress and show exact requested URL.

tests.name: chat TOCTOU: an item edited after the card is PREVIEW_STALE and nothing is written; instruction writes are diffs pinned to their revision
tests.reason: Actual edit_agent_profile approval preview must show every removed/added instruction line and refuse stale revisions before a write. Existing public card owner now includes two distant changes and an addition to an empty file, with literal changed-line oracles; retains pinned write body. Generic diff helper tests do not prove that users see the changes they approve.

tests.name: chat gate: workflow-owned chats get ADMIN_NOT_AVAILABLE and planning chats are refused, both without a card
tests.reason: Workflow-owned/planning chats must not access global Admin; denied card must write nothing; catches permission or approval bypass.

tests.name: unifiedDiff preserves distant changes and empty-file additions
tests.reason: Removed direct unifiedDiff helper execution; distant changes and additions to an empty instruction file now reach the surviving actual approval card in the TOCTOU/instructions owner. Failed unique-protection bar after consolidation. No-change formatting probe adds no separate public contract.

tests.name: chat: copying a bearer-carrying MCP server checks what it holds (by id) and flags it in red
tests.reason: Copy/enable of existing MCP must ask daemon by id for host-only bearer check and danger warning; catches bypass when agent never supplied the credential.

tests.name: chat: a plugin's MCP servers are checked with the values its files carry; install and enable both flag them
tests.reason: Plugin install/enable must inspect actual embedded MCP file credentials, show provides and warn if host-check says own bearer; catches a backdoor hidden inside plugin config.

tests.name: chat: adding a marketplace says in red that no commit is pinned and its contents cannot be shown
tests.reason: Adding marketplace must warn unpinned/unreviewed code boundary and promise per-plugin approval; catches misleading impression source content was reviewed. Drop whole title wording only. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat: an update whose kind is not the item's is refused before any card
tests.reason: Wrong-kind chat updates must reject before card/write even though external update rejects later after item read; audience timing protects truthful approvals.

tests.name: chat: the card shows the name that will be written — the adapter's keep-both name, a renamed skill's frontmatter — always pinned
tests.reason: Card must show actual keep-both/converted/renamed native name and matching frontmatter; naming change after approval must block write; catches reviewing one path while writing another.

tests.name: chat: a plugin whose directory is outside the pinned checkout says so in red on its commit row
tests.reason: Plugin outside pinned checkout must mark commit as unpinned and show danger warning; catches false supply-chain trust. Preserve flagged state/evidence rather than exact warning sentence.

tests.name: chat: a plugin with several installed versions defining one server name is flagged when ANY definition points at the daemon
tests.reason: Every installed-version MCP definition must be host-checked until a dangerous endpoint is found despite a safe provides summary; catches malicious second-version config bypass.

tests.name: chat: copies in one batch landing on one name — the second copy preview is told the first's name; without keep-both it is refused
tests.reason: Batch copies must pass earlier written names to conversion/naming, display distinct final names, and reject collisions before card when fail policy; catches overwrite or approval for wrong output name.

tests.name: chat: a batch landing on a name an earlier change deletes or renames is refused before the card (the disk cannot know yet)
tests.reason: Delete/rename/create conflicts within one batch must reject before card/writes instead of predicting stale disk name availability, while independent names still reach card; catches preview/write path mismatch.

tests.name: the box tools are chat-only; schemas refuse bad and unknown arguments
tests.reason: Each actual box tool must be unavailable to external callers and its public schema must reject malformed/unknown operation arguments before effects. Remove audiences/toolset declaration comparisons, which merely inventory current definitions; actual executeToolCall refusals remain.

tests.name: gate: a spend tool cards in every mode, for a workflow-owned chat too, and is refused while planning
tests.reason: Temporary-box spend approval is mandatory across all permission modes and workflow ownership; planning refuses. Preserve literal card kind/family/cross-project outcomes and PERMISSION_DENIED while dropping exact explanatory prose; runtime money-consent rules are independently specified by the Ephemeral AI VMs spec §13.

tests.name: create_box in full access still opens a card: the plan (cheapest provider, size, first region), its price and worst case; no grant
tests.reason: Create-box approval must show the chosen cheapest offer/provider/region, price, deadline and worst cost, then rent that exact pinned plan only after approval, preserving caller principal. Use independent literal 15 minutes for readiness timeout rather than importing the implementation constant. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: create_box: a chosen provider, size, region and time limit are checked against the offers and the provider's maximum
tests.reason: Explicit provider/size/region/lifetime choices must be validated against independently supplied offers and provider caps; invalid combinations cannot be rented.

tests.name: create_box with no provider for the kind: a clear refusal naming what to set up, and no card
tests.reason: Unavailable cloud/provider/connection/plugin configuration must return an actionable typed refusal before asking for approval or spending money.

tests.name: create_box: denied or timed out → an error and nothing created; refused while planning
tests.reason: Removed fake denied/timed-out verdict repetitions. Real approval registry owner already checks both outcomes and no machine creation; its added planning call preserves the only distinct tool-wiring refusal before a card.

tests.name: create_box from an unattended chat: the card still opens and says nobody may be watching
tests.reason: Workflow-owned and agent-triggered calls must still ask for spend approval and disclose that nobody may be watching; attended calls must not receive an incorrect unattended warning.

tests.name: create_box: a box that does not become ready is destroyed (provisioning-failed); a cancelled wait destroys it (agent)
tests.reason: A created machine that fails readiness must be destroyed with provisioning-failed; abort during readiness must destroy it as an agent cancellation, preventing abandoned paid resources.

tests.name: the card in the registry: approve rents, deny refuses with the owner's words, expiry times out, abort cancels
tests.reason: Real approval registry must hold rental until approve, create nothing on deny/timeout/abort, and keep the card pending until the specified 30-minute deadline. Replace imported timeout-derived oracle with literal 30min−1ms/pending then +1ms/timeout; catches either early or late expiry. Mock verdict tests cannot prove registry lifecycle. Absorbs the unique planning/no-card guard from the removed fake-verdict scenario.

tests.name: list_boxes and destroy_box go through the temporary-box routes
tests.reason: Box listing must normalize cost/ID fields; destroying uses the calling chat temporary-box route/reason, preserves ownership refusals and remains available during planning to stop spend.

tests.name: box_exec: defaults, the result's tails and counts, background jobs, and box_exec_output
tests.reason: Exec must map defaults and native tails/byte counts/background job IDs into the public tool shape, convert output-wait seconds to milliseconds and force the caller principal for every operation.

tests.name: box_upload / box_download: relative host paths from the chat's cwd; refusals pass through; a chat with no project is refused
tests.reason: Transfers must resolve host-relative paths from the chat cwd, preserve backend errors and refuse homeless chats instead of moving arbitrary host files.

tests.name: box_upload / box_download claim local_path: outside every project refused, another project a card below Full access
tests.reason: Both transfer directions must claim host paths before effects, refuse paths outside projects and require cross-project approval below Full access; own-project paths can reach the daemon for its containment checks.

tests.name: box_forward_port returns the host loopback URL; without the box backend every operation is BOXES_DISABLED
tests.reason: Port forwarding must expose the backend loopback URL/box port; each missing backend capability must return BOXES_DISABLED instead of throwing or simulating success.

tests.name: list_projects flattens workspaces, hides archived by default, marks recency and open sessions, recent first
tests.reason: Read/list projects must flatten workspace rows, omit archived scopes by default, expose recorded recency and count open chats; explicit archived/workspace filters must select the correct scope.

tests.name: list_projects reports a project of an archived workspace as archived (the daemon's project flag is per-project only)
tests.reason: Archived workspace status must propagate to its projects even when the daemon project flag itself is false; otherwise callers may launch archived work accidentally.

tests.name: list_projects orders recent projects newest first, then the rest alphabetically
tests.reason: Project discovery must prioritize newer recorded interactions before alphabetical unvisited projects, independently of backend row order.

tests.name: list_agents returns the catalogue, optionally one agent
tests.reason: Agent discovery must include valid chat agents, filter a named agent and reject an unknown agent with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

tests.name: list_conversations resolves the project, names each row's agent and flags resumability
tests.reason: Conversation discovery must resolve a project and preserve provider ID, account home/accountId and resumability while applying the requested limit; unknown/detect-only agents remain listed but unresumable.

tests.name: list_projects counts each project's own open sessions, terminal tabs included
tests.reason: Open-session counts must belong to each matching project and include terminal tabs, rather than counting only chats or assigning a global total.

tests.name: list_projects leaves out a workspace whose projects cannot be read and names it in warnings; the rest is listed
tests.reason: One unreadable/failed workspace must not erase other discoveries; warnings must identify the workspace and normalized failure without exposing host paths.

tests.name: a filter naming nothing that exists is refused, not answered with an empty list; an archived workspace says why it is empty
tests.reason: Unknown workspace/agent filters must be refused, while genuinely empty known/archived scopes remain honest empty answers with useful archive guidance.

tests.name: list_conversations: preview is kept, a detect-only agent's row is not resumable, and the agent filter runs before the limit
tests.reason: Conversation filtering must occur before the limit and retain preview text. Its detect-only/fourth/fifth input rows are not observed by its assertions; they can be removed without changing this unique filter-before-limit regression.

tests.name: list_conversations fails INTERNAL when the registry cannot be read, as list_agents does, instead of calling every row unresumable
tests.reason: If the registry is unavailable, discovery must fail INTERNAL rather than falsely declaring every persisted conversation unresumable.

tests.name: an empty filter is refused like any unknown one, never read as "no filter"
tests.reason: An explicitly empty workspace/agent filter must never become an omitted filter that reveals the full discovery listing; actual run and advertised schema both refuse it.

tests.name: list_agents bounds large catalogues, preserves every model and the default options, and restores named model options
tests.reason: A realistic large model catalogue must remain within the JSON-byte transport cap without dropping models unnecessarily; omitted option descriptors must be restorable by naming one model, while default model options remain available.

tests.name: list_agents reports omitted models while preserving the default and keeping a bounded result
tests.reason: A catalogue larger than the model cap must report its original size/truncation and retain the explicit default, even when that model appears deep in the source list.

tests.name: list_agents preserves launch-default options when no model has an explicit default flag
tests.reason: When the backend has no explicit default flag, the effective launch default must keep its option descriptors during size reduction.

tests.name: list_agents {agent, model}: one model with its full options; a model needs an agent, an unknown one is refused naming valid slugs
tests.reason: Named-model discovery must preserve full options including explicit legacy lookup; missing-agent/unknown-model/loading states must be distinguishable and echo bounded valid choices.

tests.name: list_conversations keeps within the result cap: 200 long rows lose the oldest ones, and truncated/omitted say how many
tests.reason: Oversize conversation discovery must keep a newest-first complete-row prefix, remain under 60000 UTF8 JSON bytes and report exact omissions; a small list must remain complete/unflagged.

tests.name: list_conversations: a row is resumable only through an ENABLED chat agent, as the GUI's resume lists require (create_session refuses a disabled one)
tests.reason: Resumability must require an enabled chat-capable agent; disabled provider conversations stay discoverable/filterable but cannot falsely advertise a resumable launch.

tests.name: list_projects: repoId per project, each workspace's git account joined from /api/accounts (label, login, provider only), query filter
tests.reason: Project discovery must expose repository identity and only safe workspace git-account label/login/provider fields; query filtering must narrow projects and workspace summaries without leaking keys or email.

tests.name: list_projects for a chat: `current` marks its project and `sameRepo` every other clone of its repository, in any workspace
tests.reason: A chat discovery must mark its own project and all other repository clones, even across workspace filters or an archived own project; no-project chats must invent neither marker.

tests.name: list_agents is the composer picker's view: the launch default (never a legacy model), chip labels, hints, option defaults; legacy only on request
tests.reason: Picker-facing discovery must independently preserve the nonlegacy launch default, chip labels, hints, option defaults, legacy opt-in, loading state and search. Remove the providerPickerView-derived oracle and duplicated provider fixture: the fixed literal assertions already protect these semantics.

tests.name: list_agents for a chat: thisThread, allowedRuntimeModes, and no email anywhere (accounts as id, label, plan, needsReauth, isDefault)
tests.reason: Chat agent discovery must expose its effective thread/model/options/mode/account and only allowed permission modes, suppress every account/provider email and preserve external-only email visibility.

tests.name: list_conversations: a chat's project defaults to its own; an external caller must name one
tests.reason: An omitted conversation project must default only for a project-bound chat; external and homeless callers must receive the correct missing-project refusal.

tests.name: list_projects below Full access (ruling S13): its own workspace whole, the others only counted; naming another workspace raises the cross-workspace metadata card
tests.reason: Below Full access project discovery must list only the own workspace, count other workspaces without reading their projects, and raise a boundary card only when another workspace is explicitly targeted; denying that card cannot expose those projects.

tests.name: send_message notify: persisted subscription with a v2 header, the new exchange at hop 1, the chip; returns at once
tests.reason: Notify must create the persisted reply subscription with literal v2 sender/project/exchange/chip metadata, return willNotify and never enter a wait route.

tests.name: send_message wait: the bound turn's reply, marked as another agent's words; a running exchange continues at hop + 1
tests.reason: Blocking reply mode must wait on the bound subscription/turn, carry the existing exchange at hop+1 and frame another agent answer with the untrusted notice.

tests.name: send_message wait: a question or the timeout goes on as notify; an empty reply says so (§13 d); a closed target too
tests.reason: Reply-router needs-input/timeout/empty/failed/closed answers must translate to distinct documented results; removed helper-computed hint wording oracle.

tests.name: send_message wait cancelled: the waiter is released through its route, once, so the reply comes as a message
tests.reason: Cancellation must release exactly the attached waiter through its route so a later reply remains deliverable as a message.

tests.name: send_message none: a working target is steered with a header asking for a send_message answer; one waiting for its user is refused
tests.reason: Fire-and-forget must steer working chats, choose answer guidance according to relative permissions and refuse steering a pending user request.

tests.name: send_message refusals: self, the exchange cap (before any route), a broader target, implementPlan while planning
tests.reason: Self-send, hop9, broader target and implement-plan while planning must refuse before any backend effect; hop8 must still be accepted.

tests.name: send_message carries plan mode on, and refuses an agent with no plan mode while planning
tests.reason: Planning messages must send interactionMode:plan to capable agents and refuse targets unable to plan.

tests.name: send_message implementPlan: the plan as the GUI's Implement sends it (no header: the host marks it implemented), chip and exchange kept
tests.reason: Implement must send the actual proposed plan with the host-recognized implementation prefix, default interaction mode and preserved provenance context.

tests.name: send_message across projects: Full access acts in its workspace; a supervised caller gets a composed boundary card, never raw arguments
tests.reason: Cross-project approval must show user message/attachment identity without base64 bytes; Full access local-workspace work remains free and workflow-owned callers refuse.

tests.name: an old host's thread_send {wait} (Task 6's real alias onto send_message): no subscription — the old steer-and-wait, a registered wait (WAIT_CYCLE)
tests.reason: The documented old-host thread_send alias must keep legacy wait-cycle protection without using new reply-subscription routes.

tests.name: send_message from an external client: notify and delegate are chat-only; wait queues behind a working session under one command id
tests.reason: External wait must queue behind a busy turn using ifIdle and the same commandId, then return only the new answer; event-subscription barriers eliminate the lost-event10s fallback.

tests.name: create_session from a chat: an opened child of this chat with its mode, model, options and account; the first turn names its sender
tests.reason: Opened-child launch must inherit caller project/mode/model/options/account, mark trusted lineage and carry sender provenance without exposing account email.

tests.name: create_session from a chat with an Agent Profile (§5.5): named by name, sent by id as an unattended launch; the result and the card name it; an unknown one is refused before any create
tests.reason: Named Agent Profiles must resolve case-insensitively to profileId for unattended launch; unknown profile must prevent session creation and omission must mean Global.

tests.name: create_session delegate: notify by default, a "Task:" title, origin delegated; another agent gets its own defaults (never a legacy model)
tests.reason: Delegation must default notify, identify delegated lineage/title and choose the requested agent nonlegacy default rather than inheriting another provider options.
