tests.name: create_session caps and refusals: a broader mode, no prompt, 6 unfinished children (GUI forks don't count), depth 2, cwd outside the project
tests.reason: Creation must refuse broader modes/missing prompt/outside cwd, enforce six unfinished agent-child slots and depth2 while excluding GUI forks.

tests.name: create_session (ported from the old delegate_task): a child opened a moment ago counts before its summary shows a turn, one that never started stops counting after its grace; depth is counted up the open tabs; a chat with no project names one
tests.reason: Fresh no-turn children must reserve slots only through the grace period, legacy parent-chain depth must count delegates but not forks, and unbound callers must name a project.

tests.name: create_session in another workspace: a boundary card showing the prompt; workflow-owned callers are denied; an inherited account gone falls back
tests.reason: Cross-workspace creation must card with the actual prompt, forbid workflow-owned requests and safely fall back from an unavailable inherited account.

tests.name: create_session card: the permission mode shown is the one the chat will get (an unknown caller mode opens the narrowest); a broader mode is refused before any card
tests.reason: The approved launch mode must be the actual selected mode even for unknown caller modes; a broader request must refuse before any card.

tests.name: create_session from an external client: project required, full-access by default, no lineage, reply none by default
tests.reason: External creation must require project, default Full access and preserve ordinary input without adding agent lineage/provenance.

tests.name: fork_session from a chat forks itself by default, marked agentCreated, finished turns only
tests.reason: Chat fork must select itself by default, mark agentCreated and translate finished-turn ordinals while rejecting running/out-of-range turns.

tests.name: merge_back_session: forks only — a delegate is told its final reply goes back by itself; a fork merges with its exchange
tests.reason: Merge-back must allow only the caller own fork, refuse delegates/parentless chats and preserve the parent exchange plus explicit delivery-resolution actions.

tests.name: plan carries on (§5.3) for create_session: a planning caller's first turn plans; an agent with no plan mode is refused before any tab opens
tests.reason: A planning create must start its first turn in plan mode; targets without plan capability must create no tab or first turn.

tests.name: plan carries on (§5.3) for merge_back_session: a planning fork's merge plans; a parent with no plan mode is refused; the parent's turn is under the turn policy
tests.reason: Planning fork merges must plan the parent turn and refuse parent agents lacking plan capability or broader parent modes before posting.

tests.name: wait_for_session from a chat: an idle session returns at once with its reply; another project's below its rights has none (§13 a)
tests.reason: Settle reads must expose own accessible replies and omit sibling content/notice below rights, retaining metadata without inappropriate cards.

tests.name: wait_for_session: an empty final reply says so; several sessions return when one settles; WAIT_CYCLE across projects
tests.reason: Empty replies must carry explicit emptyReply/hint; multi-session waits must identify the settling session and cross-project cycles must refuse.

tests.name: wait_for_session from a chat on a working chat: the bus ends the wait when it settles; the wait is registered while it lasts and released after
tests.reason: A blocking chat wait must register cycle protection while live, wake on actual bus state, return the fresh answer and release wait/listener afterward.

tests.name: wait_for_session from a chat: a cancelled wait is CANCELLED at once — listeners removed, nothing posted, the wait released
tests.reason: Cancelling a blocked chat wait must promptly return CANCELLED, release cycle state/listeners and never post into the target.

tests.name: wait_for_session from a chat: a timeout says timedOut and never stops the other chat
tests.reason: Timeout must return timedOut:true with the still-working state and release resources without interrupting the target.

tests.name: wait_for_session from an external client: attention after the cursor, timeoutSeconds, and a single session's state and reply
tests.reason: External attention waits must respect after cursors and seconds, return state/reply, and reject obsolete timeoutMs or conflicting selectors.

tests.name: external send_message parity: none steers and refuses an open request (respond_to_request named); attachments are uploaded and referenced
tests.reason: External fire-and-forget must reject pending requests, upload/reference attachments, omit agent exchange and reject invalid text/implement combinations.

tests.name: external fork_session and merge_back_session parity (§11): throughTurn, the host's refusal, the old result; resolve_merge_back as mergeId + action
tests.reason: External forks must map turn selection/host refusals without agentCreated; merges/resolutions must preserve deliberate queue errors and external trust semantics.

tests.name: cwd containment is by real paths: a link out of the sandbox or into another project is refused, for both audiences
tests.reason: Creation cwd must be validated by realpath for both audiences, refusing sandbox escapes/other-project symlinks and linked invalid project identities.

tests.name: a wait that fails after the message went out is no failed send: willNotify, and the agent is told not to send again
tests.reason: A wait failure after subscription succeeds must not report a failed send: retain queued delivery/willNotify and warn against sending again.

tests.name: a reply the waiter took whose result never reached the provider is released, so it comes again as a message
tests.reason: A reply whose tool result never reached the provider must release its waiter claim only after delivery is known to fail, ensuring fallback message delivery.

tests.name: an external wait uploads nothing for a message that is never sent, and posts nothing once cancelled
tests.reason: External wait must avoid uploads for unsent messages and never retry posting after cancellation, preventing orphaned bytes/late side effects.

tests.name: a failed wait is worded by why: a message follows only for WAIT_CYCLE / HOST_UNAVAILABLE; another wait or a gone subscription says so
tests.reason: Post-send failure classification must distinguish recoverable cycle/restart notify from consumed/gone/unknown waits and prevent duplicate message guidance.

tests.name: a delegate's final reply is its result, delivered to the parent; the delegate is refused merge-back
tests.reason: Real ReplyRouter/LineageService must automatically deliver a delegate final answer once while refusing explicit merge-back; no remaining real-route scenario covers delegate delivery.

tests.name: get_desktops resolves the project to its path, and lists every project's desktops without one
tests.reason: Desktop discovery must resolve workspace/project to the daemon projectPath query, omit that query for global external listing and reject a nonexistent project.

tests.name: get_desktops {desktopId} finds the desktop in the full list; an unknown id is NOT_FOUND with a hint; host adds the host status
tests.reason: Desktop-ID lookup must select the requested desktop; host prerequisites must be read for that desktop/project and degrade only expected offline-VM errors while preserving unrelated backend refusals and argument constraints.

tests.name: get_desktops {desktopId, appId} returns the log, a JSON-looking log as text, and the tail of an oversized one
tests.reason: App logs must remain text even when JSON-looking, preserve the newest complete-character tail inside the byte cap and retain the correct missing-app refusal.

tests.name: control_desktop open posts the project path, the options and a first app; cwd or env without a command is refused first
tests.reason: Opening desktops must map project/options/first-app fields to their shared daemon API and reject meaningless cwd/env-without-command before any POST.

tests.name: control_desktop's fields per action, and the schema's limits
tests.reason: Action-specific required/forbidden arguments and public command/env/size limits must be enforced before a desktop operation; obsolete unsupported actions remain invalid. Size checks here validate a request contract, not rendered geometry.

tests.name: a DESKTOP_UNAVAILABLE refusal carries the daemon's install hint
tests.reason: A desktop-unavailable refusal must retain the host-supplied installation hint so the caller can tell the owner which prerequisite is missing; full sentence punctuation is incidental.

tests.name: control_desktop launch_app, stop_app (force=1 only when forced), close_window and close reach their routes
tests.reason: Each supported desktop operation must target its documented route/ID and map force only when requested, returning normalized stopped/closed/launch outcomes.

tests.name: chat: open and launch_app are Admin — a card naming the command, the working directory and every env value in full
tests.reason: Host process launch must always require Admin approval with the exact agent-written command/cwd/env values and loader warning; only eligible full-access project grants may suppress subsequent equivalent launch cards. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat: stop_app, close_window and close are Act — no card in the own project; a card in another workspace
tests.reason: Stopping desktop processes must remain an Act operation in the own project, require cross-workspace approval where appropriate and be unavailable while planning. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat: a cwd outside every project is refused; a workflow-owned chat cannot open; the own project is the default
tests.reason: Host process launch cwd must remain within a project; workflow-owned chats cannot start Admin host processes, and the own project is the default target for project-bound chats.

tests.name: chat: another workspace's desktops are a metadata read (card below Full access); an app's log is content
tests.reason: Desktop metadata and app log content must claim different read scopes so below-Full-access cross-workspace reads are carded while legitimate own/same-workspace reads proceed.

tests.name: desktop card: the loader-key warning covers loaders, runtimes, shells, git hooks and GUI plugins; values stay in full
tests.reason: Every supported native loader/runtime/shell/git/plugin environment key must be named in an execution warning while all agent-written values remain fully visible, including long ones; benign keys/no env must not generate false loader warnings.

tests.name: read_file on a directory lists it (list_files' successor) inside one result: the first entries by name, truncated:true
tests.reason: Directory reads return an alphabetical whole-entry prefix within one JSON result and honestly flag omitted entries. A large directory response loses JSON metadata, splits an entry or claims completeness after dropping names. FsTools only caps entry count; this MCP owner handles serialized-result fitting and directory-via-read_file behavior. Oracle: Actual directory with known long names, independent alphabetical expected prefix and literal 60000-byte JSON ceiling.

tests.name: read_file shortens a default window that would not fit one result, and paging from nextOffset reads the file exactly
tests.reason: Default file window shrinks for serialization overhead and successive nextOffset pages reconstruct the original bytes exactly. A normal large file loses/duplicates bytes because paging assumes offset+maxBytes after a shortened window. Filesystem byte-window tests do not include MCP JSON serialization overhead or the public nextOffset contract. Oracle: Actual file contents, independently counted result bytes and byte-exact concatenation through returned nextOffset.

tests.name: read_file stays inside one result even for escape-heavy text and the largest window
tests.reason: The maximum allowed read window also fits when text expands through JSON escaping, with advancing lossless pages. The largest window with quote/backslash/control content exceeds the result budget or shrinking loops without advancing. Default-window plain text does not exercise worst-case escaping and maximum schema window. Oracle: Actual escape-heavy file, largest public maxBytes, independent serialized byte count and exact source reconstruction.

tests.name: read_file never splits a character: nextOffset is where the page's text ends, and the pages concatenate byte-exactly
tests.reason: UTF-8 windows never split a character; nextOffset is consumed bytes and even a smaller-than-character window advances while concatenating byte-exactly. CJK characters are corrupted/skipped/duplicated at a page edge or a tiny window loops forever. ASCII/escape-heavy paging has single-byte characters and cannot reveal UTF-8 boundary/consumption errors. Oracle: Literal multibyte file, no replacement characters, independent Buffer.byteLength/three-byte boundary and full source equality, explicit offset/maxBytes examples.

tests.name: read_file for a chat: a path inside its project reads (relative to its directory); a directory lists; outside every project is PERMISSION_DENIED
tests.reason: Chat relative paths resolve from cwd, project directory reads work, and nonproject/traversal/symlink escape targets are denied. An agent reads workspace-adjacent or outside-project secrets through cwd confusion or symlink traversal. FsTools sandbox alone allows workspace-adjacent files; this uniquely exercises the chat project gate and relative-cwd semantics. Oracle: Actual temporary project/files/symlink with known bytes and specific PERMISSION_DENIED at each forbidden target through executeToolCall.

tests.name: read_file for a chat: another project's content follows the gate (same workspace under auto: allowed; another workspace: a card, refused without a port)
tests.reason: Cross-project file content obeys runtime policy: same-workspace auto allowed, supervised requires approval, cross-workspace auto requires approval, full access allowed. A project read bypasses approval policy or full-access/same-workspace allowed content is incorrectly denied. Sandbox/path containment tests cannot exercise project classification and caller runtime policy decisions. Oracle: Actual files in separate projects/workspaces with distinct literal contents; actual executor has no approval port and returns explicit refusal for card-required cases.

tests.name: read_file for an external caller keeps the sandbox rule only: relative to the sandbox root, anywhere inside it
tests.reason: External reads remain relative to the sandbox root and reject traversal for the sandbox reason; missing DaemonApi file capability fails UNAVAILABLE. External read escapes the root or an absent transport capability secretly falls back to local disk. Chat project policy is stricter and cannot protect the external sandbox compatibility contract; typed refusal replaces a baseline bare rejects false-positive. Oracle: Actual root.txt fixture, FsSandboxError specifically for traversal, and explicit UNAVAILABLE from a capability-free API.

tests.name: get_git_state status: the project's status with its file list capped (filesTruncated, omittedFiles)
tests.reason: Git status resolves canonical project, preserves branch/upstream/ahead/behind and bounds changed-file rows honestly; nonrepositories remain explicit. A caller sees status for the wrong project or an apparently complete file list after dropping changes. Git service tests own status extraction; this solely owns MCP canonical addressing and truncation metadata. Oracle: Literal acme/api request query and backend status fields, 300-row prefix with independent omitted-count arithmetic, isRepo:false fixture.

tests.name: get_git_state branches and log: lists capped; the log asks for `limit` commits, clips bodies and fits one result
tests.reason: Branches/log cap whole rows; log forwards limit/default and bounds individual bodies plus total result without dropping newest commits first. History ignores the requested limit or oversized commit bodies overflow the result and lose metadata/order. Status/diff byte paths contain no commits, and generic JSON truncation cannot preserve whole commits/newest-first. Oracle: Literal request limit100/default20, known ordered commits, independent 60000-byte count, body bounds and uncut small response.

tests.name: get_git_state diff: the working diff cut to one result with untracked files capped; one file's diff by repo-relative path, staged or not
tests.reason: Working diff and untracked rows fit one result with truthful daemon truncation; file diff accepts only project-contained paths and sends repo-relative staged selection. A large diff is silently incomplete, staged requests read unstaged data or a path escapes its project. Status/log do not exercise diff text fitting, staged wire query or single-file project containment. Oracle: Independent huge diff/untracked fixtures and byte count; literal src/a.ts, staged query, daemon truncated flag and explicit invalid outside/root paths.

tests.name: get_git_state defaults to the chat project, requires an external project, and rejects ignored arguments before approval
tests.reason: Real executor calls must default a chat to its own project, demand an external project and reject ignored path/staged fields before approval. Literal project/error field oracles protect tool scope argument semantics absent from Git service tests.

tests.name: knowledge_search: posts the query with the calling session; compact hits with collection names, one-line snippets and citations
tests.reason: Visible search results carry the caller principal, normalized query/collection selection, entry citations and compact concept hits. A search omits sessionId and leaks or searches another visibility scope; citations or snippets disappear during projection. Only this case tests search request normalization and both entry/concept result projection; store/search algorithm tests cannot exercise MCP projection. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: The literal chat-1 request body, fixture collection names, entry ID and citation supplied by the backend, and whitespace-normalized literal snippet.

tests.name: knowledge_search: nothing found says so; the limits are the contract's
tests.reason: No matches must be reported honestly; empty/oversize query, invalid limit/ref and caller-supplied session identity are refused. The tool produces a plausible knowledge answer after no hits or sends an invalid/untrusted principal to the daemon. The positive search projection case cannot catch an empty-result lie or invalid query/identity acceptance; max-accepted values have a separate boundary owner. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: An empty backend hit list and expected INVALID_ARGUMENT for concrete bad inputs, using separately owned daemon/search and API limits.

tests.name: knowledge_get: the entry whole with its citation, concepts and related entries; the session in the query; a long body is cut
tests.reason: Read an entry with intact body, ready-made citation, URL, concepts, related citations and caller visibility; long UTF-8 bodies remain within one result. Entry reading loses lines/citation/visibility or a multibyte large body overflows the public result budget. Search deliberately returns snippets only; this is the sole entry-detail body/related-entry and entry-byte-budget owner. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Literal two-line body, citation/related metadata supplied as backend data, literal sessionId query and independent 60000-byte ceiling.

tests.name: knowledge_get: a concept — description, entries, links; a hidden or unknown id is the daemon's refusal
tests.reason: A concept read exposes description, aliases, attributes, related entries and directed graph links; hidden IDs retain KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND. Concept results omit usable graph information or turn a visibility refusal into successful empty content. Entry-detail rendering is a different union arm and cannot catch concept/link projection; search has only compact concepts. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Literal concept/edge/neighbor fixture and explicit KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND code from the daemon response.

tests.name: knowledge_save: one call, many items, the session named, handles without @; no card, even while planning
tests.reason: Bulk save uses one request scoped to the chat, normalizes handles/collections, reports duplicate/created collection outcomes, and needs no card even in plan mode. Saving is blocked during planning, requests approval, forges identity, sends @-prefixed handles, or misreports duplicate entries as newly saved. Store deduplication owns persistence; this is the tool normalization, plan-safe execution and caller-facing bulk outcome owner. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Literal expected bulk wire payload and independent saved/duplicate/created collection response fixture; actual executor has no approval port.

tests.name: knowledge_save: inputs mirror the contract — at least one collection, body and count caps, strict items; the daemon's refusals pass through
tests.reason: Save refuses empty/missing collection/body, count/byte overflow and extra item keys; backend plugin/validation failures remain typed. Malformed bulk content reaches persistence or a daemon refusal is reported as a successful save. Successful bulk save cannot catch input acceptance or error forwarding; max-accepted metadata has its own off-by-one boundary case. Oracle: Concrete invalid payloads plus independently owned API count/byte limits and explicit daemon error code assertions.

tests.name: knowledge_update: PATCHes only the fields passed (null clears, no @, collections once), names the session, answers what changed and the citation; no card
tests.reason: Knowledge tools spec requires PATCHing only supplied fields, explicit null clearing, normalized handles/deduplicated collections, caller session identity and an answer naming changed fields/citation without echoing body text. Preserve literal wire body and result data while removing ordered heading/punctuation freezes; store tests do not exercise MCP projection.

tests.name: knowledge_update: an id, at least one change and the save limits; the daemon's refusals pass through
tests.reason: Knowledge update API requires an entry id, at least one change, strict fields and save-compatible value limits. Invalid requests must cause no PATCH; hidden entries preserve KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND. Literal bad inputs/error codes prove this tool boundary independently of backend validation.

tests.name: knowledge_delete: reads then deletes each id once, with the session; reports each deleted or not; nothing deleted is the daemon's refusal
tests.reason: Knowledge delete API requires one deletion per unique id, visibility-aware lookup with caller session identity, per-entry successful/refused status and daemon error when none delete. Preserve exact side-effect requests and per-id status data while removing whole-sentence grammar snapshots; backend deletion tests cannot verify MCP batching/result/error projection.

tests.name: knowledge_collections: every collection by name, count and description
tests.reason: Collection discovery supplies every name, entry count, description, total/unfiled count and actionable empty-state guidance. An agent cannot choose the correct collection because a row or its metadata is missing or an empty result is misleading. Search only names searched collections and has no discovery totals/descriptions or empty-create guidance. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Two literal collection rows and literal 52 total/3 unfiled counts supplied by an independent backend response.

tests.name: worker tools: next task (instructions once, then a pointer), submit returns the next one; an invalid answer is refused to be redone
tests.reason: Worker next/submit forwards session/task/answer, renders initial instructions then the prior-task pointer, returns the next task, refuses an invalid answer and reports stop. A worker loses task instructions or identity, advances despite rejection, or keeps processing after a done response. Worker broker tests own task validity and parsing; this uniquely owns their MCP wire/result/error projection across the worker protocol. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Literal task IDs/instructions/answer and explicit accepted/refused/done backend responses; fake parsing selects a response but does not implement rendering or error conversion.

tests.name: worker tools: a chat that is no worker gets the daemon's KNOWLEDGE_NOT_A_WORKER as a clean error
tests.reason: A nonworker receives the daemon KNOWLEDGE_NOT_A_WORKER refusal; empty task ID/answer or missing answer is INVALID_ARGUMENT. An unauthorized chat sees an apparently successful worker task or malformed submission is accepted. The happy worker progression never exercises a 403 identity refusal or submission schema failures. Oracle: Fixed 403 backend error code and concrete empty/missing input payloads.

tests.name: the family is chat-only: an external caller is never served it
tests.reason: External credentials cannot use the chat-only knowledge search boundary. An external caller is admitted to session-scoped knowledge without a chat principal. Route visibility tests require a principal and do not prove catalog audience enforcement; this represents the family audience restriction through an actual tool call, not a declaration inventory. Oracle: Actual executor result TOOL_NOT_FOUND and zero backend calls for an external caller.

tests.name: knowledge inputs accept exactly the daemon's limits (query, kind, author, handle)
tests.reason: The tool accepts query/kind/author/handle values exactly at the daemon-supported limits, including @ before handle normalization. An unnecessary stricter MCP bound rejects valid data accepted by daemon search/store. Oversize-refusal cases detect permissive bounds only; this catches off-by-one overrestriction and handle normalization before counting. Oracle: Separately owned daemon validation/search limits, with successful public executor calls at those exact boundaries.

tests.name: knowledge_get: a concept's text fields are bounded — a text result is not capped by the executor
tests.reason: Unbounded concept graph fields and lists are reduced to a usable text result under 60000 bytes without losing concept identity or omitted-item guidance. A large graph concept bypasses the executor JSON limiter and floods the agent context or drops all useful identity. Entry byte trimming cannot constrain aliases/attributes/neighbors; generic executor caps do not apply to this text result. Rewritten around backend IDs/citation/body/input bytes and semantic state/order/budget; punctuation/heading freezes removed. Oracle: Independently counted UTF-8 result bytes below literal 60000 plus retained tactic-x/alias identity and a visible omission count.

tests.name: fork_session forks through a transcript turn number and returns the new session
tests.reason: Fork through a transcript turn uses transcript numbering including zero-before-first, unattended launch and a new command ID, returning the new session. Fork copies the wrong turn/role, includes unwanted turns or launches an attended interaction instead of the requested new tab. Host fork logic owns actual copying; only this adapter case checks transcript-number to wire-cut conversion and returned MCP session. Oracle: Literal t1/t2 IDs, user/assistant roles and expected fork route body for throughTurn 0/1/default; backend new-session result.

tests.name: fork_session refuses a turn past the end, and passes the host's refusal through
tests.reason: An out-of-range turn is INVALID_ARGUMENT and a host command refusal retains its code. Invalid transcript cut creates a fork, or a genuine host refusal is mislabeled as success. Valid cuts do not exercise either client preflight or daemon failure mapping. Oracle: Explicit invalid turn number and literal COMMAND_REJECTED response, with asserted error codes.

tests.name: fork_session profile (Agent Profiles §5.5): by name or id, null or "global" for Global, omitted inherits; the result reports it
tests.reason: Profile names and IDs resolve; null/global explicitly clear; omission inherits; the response identifies the resulting profile. A fork silently runs Global instead of the selected/inherited profile or sends the display name where the route requires ID. Profile-store tests resolve persisted records but do not prove fork omission/clearing or MCP result profile projection. Oracle: Literal p-growth/name mapping and independent expected profileId wire bodies for explicit, null/global and omitted values.

tests.name: fork_session profile refusals: an unknown one is refused before anything is forked; a profile the daemon cannot prepare fails naming it
tests.reason: Unknown/deleted/unready fork profiles fail without silently falling back; errors identify the profile and no initial fork is posted for an unknown name. A user-requested or inherited constrained profile is dropped and a more permissive Global fork is created. The positive profile-selection case cannot catch missing/deleted inherited profiles or dishonest fallback behavior. Oracle: Explicit missing-name zero-POST check and independent PROFILE_NOT_READY/PROFILE_NOT_FOUND daemon refusals with named profile context.

tests.name: fork_session continues in another agent: its model (named, else its default), options and account
tests.reason: Continuing in another agent uses that agent model/default, options and account and reports transcript strategy/handoff. The new provider is handed the parent provider model/account/options or inherits its default unintentionally. Same-agent native forking follows another path; provider launch tests do not cover the fork adapter target resolution/handoff result. Oracle: Distinct literal Claude/Codex model IDs, target default and expected refId/accountId/modelSelection wire bodies.

tests.name: fork_session on the same agent: a model alone forks natively on it; another account continues by transcript
tests.reason: Same-agent model changes preserve compatible options and native strategy; account changes request transcript continuation. An account-changing fork tries an incompatible native resume or a model-only fork discards valid options. Cross-agent continuation always chooses a new provider default and cannot catch preserving same-agent state or account-only continuation. Oracle: Literal source/target model and account IDs, expected modelSelection and independent native/transcript response strategies.

tests.name: fork_session refuses an unknown or unavailable agent, a model or account it does not have — before anything is forked
tests.reason: Unknown/disabled agents and foreign model/account/options are refused before creating any fork. Invalid provider selections cause a partially created or wrongly configured chat. Valid native/cross-agent cases cannot prove atomic refusal before launch. Oracle: Concrete foreign/disabled selections, typed INVALID_ARGUMENT assertions and no POST observation.

tests.name: merge_back_session sends the fork's text and reports the delivery; a session that is no fork is refused
tests.reason: A fork sends its result to its parent through merge-back and reports delivery; a nonfork cannot use merge-back. Fork output is lost/sent to the wrong parent or an unrelated/delegated chat is treated as a fork. Host delivery tests cannot prove the MCP fork-only precondition and text/route projection. Oracle: Literal merge text, command route and independent delivery/lineage fixture; nonfork expected INVALID_ARGUMENT with no POST.

tests.name: fork_session re-sends the SAME commandId while the host restarts, so a retry is one fork
tests.reason: HOST_UNAVAILABLE retry of a fork reuses the same command ID, creating one logical fork. A host handover causes the tool to create two forks after an ambiguous first attempt. General command retry ownership alone does not prove this side-effecting fork caller uses the idempotent path. Oracle: A first 503 followed by success, two actual fork requests whose nonempty commandId is equal, and one returned created session.

tests.name: resolve_merge_back is merge_back_session {mergeId, action}: deliver or discard a pending merge
tests.reason: Deliver/discard of a queued merge is exposed as merge_back_session with mergeId/action. A queued merge action posts a new merge instead of resolving the existing delivery or selects the wrong action. Sending a new merge uses a different endpoint and cannot catch pending-item routing. Oracle: Literal pending merge ID, correct item route and independently expected deliver/discard request/result.

tests.name: send_message posts the turn body, waits for the new turn and returns its reply
tests.reason: Literal POST input/mode and new turn t2/reply hello prove dispatch-to-return correlation, independent of fake's posted flag; old-host thread_send compatibility path is intentional §14.1.

tests.name: send_message without wait returns sent; attachments are uploaded first and referenced
tests.reason: Uploaded attachment ID must be referenced in the outgoing turn and outcome sent returned immediately; fake upload supplies ID but does not construct the tool's request.

tests.name: send_message refusals: empty, pending request, plan mode unsupported; an errored session is sent to
tests.reason: Empty/unsupported-plan refusal must post nothing; error/stopped sessions remain restartable. Title's pending-request mention is not executed here; dedicated pending owner below covers it.

tests.name: send_message reports needs-input with the pending requests, and timeout
tests.reason: Real send wait must return actual pending r1 as needs-input, and bounded silent wait timeout; fake only supplies remote state, not outcome classification.

tests.name: implement_plan sends the prefixed plan in default mode; refuses without an actionable plan
tests.reason: Plan text must be trimmed/prefixed exactly as GUI implement operation, default mode used, no-plan refused; aliases map to current send_message implementPlan API deliberately.

tests.name: implement_plan sends the FULL plan: a plan slimmed on the wire is read back unslimmed, never sent cut
tests.reason: A wire-truncated plan must be refetched whole and sent intact; unavailable full item must refuse with no POST. Ordinary small plan cannot detect partial-plan implementation.

tests.name: implement_plan judges the plan on the fresh snapshot (the host's rule), not on the summary one poll behind
tests.reason: Fresh snapshot actionability must override stale summary both directions, avoiding duplicate plan execution or refusal of a newly proposed plan.

tests.name: send_message: a needs-input the snapshot does not confirm is the summary's lag, and the wait goes on
tests.reason: Unconfirmed needs-input must keep waiting without busy reads, then bus completion return t2/done; stale metadata is not a legitimate request outcome.

tests.name: send_message: a wait on a flag the snapshot never confirms still ends — at the timeout, on a close, on an abort
tests.reason: Stale-flag waits must terminate on timeout/close/abort and remove bus listeners; each outcome has distinct lifetime/error semantics and prevents a hung MCP call.

tests.name: send_message: PENDING_REQUEST names each open request and respond_to_request, never the removed tools
tests.reason: PENDING_REQUEST must identify actual r1/q1 and current respond_to_request remediation, with no removed tool recommendations; IDs are caller-actionable public error data.

tests.name: read_transcript accepts maxChars through 55000 with a 40000-byte default
tests.reason: Public read_transcript input schema must default40000 and allow55000/refuse55001; fixed documented byte limits are not private implementation constants.

tests.name: send_message: the baseline is read right before the POST, so a turn that ended during the upload is not this message's
tests.reason: A turn ending during upload must be part of the pre-POST baseline, so later t3/NEW answers the send instead of old t2; upload timing is an actual independent race.

tests.name: send_message never returns an earlier turn's id or reply: a provider that fails to (re)start
tests.reason: Provider failure before a new/queued turn starts must return failed without earlier t1 ID/text; normal completed waits cannot protect restart failure correlation.

tests.name: send_message refusals upload nothing; plan mode needs a known capability
tests.reason: Pending request or unreadable plan capabilities must refuse before uploads or POST; rejection code alone would not detect irreversible upload side effects.

tests.name: send_message: with no bus event at all, a stale needs-input is rechecked and the completed reply returned
tests.reason: Without bus notification, controlled2-second recheck must notice completion and return t2/done, preserving progress despite a missed publication.

tests.name: send_message: a stale park never outlives the timeout — the last one is only what is left of it
tests.reason: A recheck park must use remaining deadline, not a fresh2-second interval; virtual2999/3000-ms boundaries protect the caller timeout.

tests.name: send_message: a turn that ended during the upload is over even when only the summary knows it — a failed next turn returns no old reply
tests.reason: Summary-only settled baseline plus subsequent provider failure must omit old t2 reply; complements snapshot-baseline race rather than duplicating it.

tests.name: send_message: a running turn stamped with a mid-turn completedAt is not over — a steer into it gets its reply
tests.reason: Running state wins over a mid-turn completedAt checkpoint stamp; steered work keeps t2 and returns its eventual answer rather than treating it already settled.

tests.name: send_message: the list catching up on a turn that was already over is not this message's outcome — the wait goes on to its own turn
tests.reason: A stale list catching up to preexisting settled t2 cannot terminate the new wait; only subsequent t3/NEW answers this message.

tests.name: read_transcript includes its truncation hint within the byte budget when only the roster is trimmed
tests.reason: Roster-only transcript trimming must keep requested message entries, flags and nonempty hint within2000 bytes; row-budget calculation excluding hint otherwise exceeds cap.

tests.name: send_message planMode on a degraded 200 providers body: the capability could not be read, and the refusal says so
tests.reason: Degraded200 provider body must fail plan request closed, with no POST; unavailable503 and typed unsupported provider use distinct parsing/reliability paths.

tests.name: read_transcript refuses an empty agentId rather than answering the main view
tests.reason: Empty public agentId must fail schema instead of falling through to root transcript; valid task ID remains accepted, preventing wrong-scope reads.

tests.name: send_message's result keeps within the cap beside a full detail: the pending request it returns twice is paid for by the subagent list
tests.reason: After a send, duplicated pending data plus full detail must still fit60000 and keep request/reply whole while trimming roster; session-detail-alone budgeting cannot protect this outer frame.

tests.name: send_message: a reply too wide for one result beside a wide plan is cut by bytes, on a code-point boundary, and comes back as `reply` with replyTruncated — the plan kept whole
tests.reason: Large UTF8 reply must be returned once with replyTruncated, keep whole plan and fit result for external and legacy shapes; wrappers have different frame overhead.

tests.name: read_transcript: beforeTurn past turnCount + 1 is refused naming the range, one below 2 by the schema — before any page is read
tests.reason: beforeTurn input/range must reject before paging and permit turnCount+1 latest window; fixed coveredTurns9,10 protects ordinal interpretation.

tests.name: read_transcript: with turns named unavailable, the answer — its hint, and the shed hint after it — still fits maxChars
tests.reason: Unavailable-turn and trimming hints must be included in maxChars across concrete budgets with unavailableTurns preserved; text-only cap is insufficient.

tests.name: read_transcript: a subagent of an older turn is known by the rows a page brought back
tests.reason: An older-page child absent from retained roster must be recognized from retrieved rows and return only its words; truly absent child must refuse.

tests.name: read_transcript: a workflow member's id, ":wf:" and all, drills into its own rows and is validated like any other
tests.reason: A workflow member ID containing :wf: must drill into only that member's rows and reject missing slot; ordinary agent IDs do not exercise compound identity.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a Codex /goal status runs on the host — no turn wait, and the status row is the answer
tests.reason: Host-run Codex goal status posts normalized command but starts no turn wait, returning goal/answer/seq with no reply/turnId; Claude uses different routing.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a goal update answers /goal <objective>, with the rest of the same command
tests.reason: Replacement goal's cleared and later set sibling rows must join one command answer after settle window; first update alone must not return partial result.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a failed goal command is outcome failed, and the answer says why
tests.reason: Goal failure activity must produce failed outcome with reason text; normal turn-error handling cannot classify host-command activity answers.

tests.name: goals §5.1: only rows after the command's own message answer it, and a hidden progress tick never does
tests.reason: Only rows following this command's own user message answer it; old achievement and hidden progress cannot be mistaken for its status answer.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a command that writes no row comes back without an answer once the wait runs out
tests.reason: No-row host goal command must end without fabricated answer and supply hint; a correct status-row success does not prevent indefinite wait on idempotent commands.

tests.name: goals §5.1: wait:false posts a host /goal and returns sent, as for any message
tests.reason: Host goal reply:none must post once and immediately return sent without answer; goal wait logic must not override explicit no-wait caller intent.

tests.name: goals §5.1: an open request holds back every message but a /goal the host runs
tests.reason: Host-run goal pause bypasses pending-card send block while preserving actual pending request; normal prompts and provider-run Claude goals remain blocked.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a /goal whose route cannot be told — the capabilities unread — is refused, as plan mode is
tests.reason: Unreadable goal capabilities must refuse command routing before POST, while ordinary text remains sendable; otherwise call waits on a turn the host never starts.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a host /goal with attachments is refused before anything is uploaded or posted
tests.reason: Host goal with attachments must refuse before upload/POST; attachments are unsupported command data and must not trigger side effects before validation.

tests.name: goals §5.1: on Claude a /goal is an ordinary prompt, waited on as a turn
tests.reason: Claude /goal is a normal agent prompt yielding t2/completed/reply, not a host goal answer; provider capability controls route, not slash spelling alone.

tests.name: goals §5.1: the answer window runs from when the session is up — a cold session's start never eats it
tests.reason: Cold session startup must not consume goal answer window; controlled20-second startup still waits and returns eventual real status row.

tests.name: goals §5.1: a pause of a paused goal, or a resume of an active one, waits a settle's worth, not the whole window
tests.reason: Already-paused pause/already-active resume end after settling with no answer; state-changing pause still waits. Fixed statuses and virtual clock prove selective early completion.

tests.name: goals §5.1: an answer is cut by bytes, and says so, so the result keeps its cap
tests.reason: Huge multibyte goal answer must retain recognizable prefix, answerTruncated and8192-byte bound while whole result fits60000; character count alone overflows wire.

tests.name: goals §5.7: a deploy's hold row is no answer: /goal status settles on its own status row
tests.reason: Deploy heldForUpdate status row must not answer user's goal status; wait continues until user's actual status row, avoiding unrelated handover text returned as command result.

tests.name: notify_user posts the push for the calling chat (its own session), in every mode and while planning
tests.reason: Chat notifications use the calling session identity and remain usable in ordinary, planning and workflow-owned callers; external calls carry no session ID. A notification is attributed to another tab or blocked by unnecessary tool approval/planning policy. Push service tests own delivery; this uniquely proves MCP attribution and catalog gate execution. The title overstates every runtime mode; the body exercises the three listed caller configurations. Oracle: Actual executor succeeds without approval port; literal POST bodies have sessionId me for three independently configured callers and no identity externally.

tests.name: notify_user: caps are the contract's, and the daemon's RATE_LIMITED passes through
tests.reason: Push title/body limits and nonspoofable identity are enforced; RATE_LIMITED retains retry guidance; invisible titles consume no push quota. Oversize/empty/control-only notifications are sent or rate-limit information is swallowed. Successful notify projection cannot catch schema/sanitization preflight or typed daemon refusal. Oracle: Concrete bad title/body/sessionId inputs, literal RATE_LIMITED and 300-second backend guidance, unchanged backend-call count for sanitized-empty input.

tests.name: a running shell grows between two pages: the next page continues at the last one's end, until it finishes
tests.reason: Preserve actual host fold/log/retention to read_transcript/read_tool_output chain, source-byte reconstruction and running/complete status. Register host.stop as test teardown immediately so assertion failures also release host resources; no normal-run speedup is claimed. Mock-window tests cannot prove evicted durable output or live incremental joins.

tests.name: past the cap a running command loses its start — sixteen later calls of its agent, all more recently active, hold the slots — so its latest chunk is the entry and the id, and its whole output reads back from the log
tests.reason: Preserve actual host fold/log/retention to read_transcript/read_tool_output chain, source-byte reconstruction and running/complete status. Register host.stop as test teardown immediately so assertion failures also release host resources; no normal-run speedup is claimed. Mock-window tests cannot prove evicted durable output or live incremental joins.

tests.name: read_tool_output validates byte-window bounds and applies documented defaults
tests.reason: The public byte-window schema must default offset0/maxBytes40000 and reject out-of-range or empty identifiers.

tests.name: a message answers its text, and any other item the GUI viewer's text: a string payload as it is, else indented JSON, else the summary
tests.reason: Messages/string payload/JSON payload/fallback summary must expose the actual requested full text rather than command-only previews.

tests.name: windows are UTF-8 byte windows that never split a character, and chain through nextOffset to the end
tests.reason: UTF8 byte windows must be resumable, align interior offsets and include a whole wide character even at tiny limits; long default cap behavior remains.

tests.name: an offset at the end reads nothing more; one past it is refused, naming totalBytes
tests.reason: EOF must return empty text and past-end offsets must fail INVALID_ARGUMENT with recoverable totalBytes.

tests.name: every answer stays within the result cap: an escape-heavy window at the largest maxBytes comes back shorter
tests.reason: Escape-heavy/control/CJK outputs must be paged under60000 serialized bytes without losing any source bytes.

tests.name: an item the host does not have is NOT_FOUND, saying where item ids come from; any other failure keeps its code
tests.reason: Missing items must map to NOT_FOUND with a usable item-id source; deliberate other host failures retain their error codes.

tests.name: only a chat session's items are read: an unknown session and a terminal tab are refused before any item read
tests.reason: Only open chat sessions may expose item output, and item IDs containing slashes/colons must be encoded as one route segment.

tests.name: the item's own unslimmed output takes precedence over the streamed copy
tests.reason: An intact item own full output must take precedence over a potentially stale streamed copy.

tests.name: `${host}: a running call answers its output so far with running: true, and says truncated when the host's cap cut it`
tests.reason: Both whole-join and windowing hosts must report running/truncated flags and retain all escaped bytes under the result cap.

tests.name: `${host}: a stored-slimmed update is never command-output: its data is the preview — the join answers, else its payload`
tests.reason: A stored slim update cannot be mislabeled as whole command output: real join wins, otherwise expose stored payload.

tests.name: `${host}: a completion that kept only its output's head reads the call's join — never the head as the whole output`
tests.reason: A completion that retained only a head must prefer the full streamed join and avoid claiming the head is complete.

tests.name: `${host}: with no join to give — nothing streamed, or no route — a completion's kept head answers as command-output, truncated`
tests.reason: Without a usable join, retained completion head must remain readable as explicitly truncated command output.

tests.name: `${host}: an OpenCode completion whose output the tool cut reads the join; with none, the part it kept — its END — answers, truncated`
tests.reason: OpenCode retained output is a tail with a saved-file note: join wins if available, otherwise preserve that actual tail and truncation.

tests.name: `${host}: a host without the join — an older one's route miss, or its own 404 — falls back to the item's text, never an error`
tests.reason: Old-host route404/item404 must fall back safely; unavailable/malformed join answers must preserve meaningful failure codes.

tests.name: `${host}: a live Claude Bash call streams its result's text as a command's output: a result given as blocks reads back through the join`
tests.reason: Claude block-array Bash results must expose streamed command text from the join rather than JSON tool_result blocks.

tests.name: `${host}: a file change is never command-output: a Write whose result streamed as file_change_output answers its payload`
tests.reason: File-change results/output chunks must remain payloads, while command-output chunks must follow the command join path.

tests.name: `${host}: an offset at the end of the join reads nothing more; one past it is refused, naming totalBytes`
tests.reason: Both host protocols must accept EOF but reject all past-end offsets, including huge values without unsafe exponential queries.

tests.name: a windowing host and a host that ignores the window answer the same pages, byte for byte, at every window size
tests.reason: Whole-join and windowing-host pages must agree byte-for-byte for mixed Unicode, escapes, lone surrogates and controls at narrow/wide windows; redundant alignment cycles removed.

tests.name: a window the host could not have cut is INTERNAL: out of place, past maxBytes or totalBytes, empty before the end
tests.reason: Impossible host windows must reject as INTERNAL; valid interior-offset character rounding and EOF must remain accepted.

tests.name: answer_question encodes single, multi (values over labels), custom text and index keys, and posts one /answer
tests.reason: Responding to all questions maps IDs/indexes and option label to value, encodes single/multi/custom/secret external answers and issues one answer command. The provider receives display labels instead of option values, the wrong question IDs or an attachment field despite no files. Provider adapters own consuming answers; only this tool test proves MCP answer-key/value normalization and route projection. Oracle: Literal expected answers keyed by Which database?/Modules/Token, q1 request ID, seq30 and returned c1 session.

tests.name: answer_question: custom text where allowed, wrapped single→multi, unwrapped one-element arrays, case-insensitive labels
tests.reason: Custom text, case-insensitive options and scalar/one-element-array convenience forms normalize to the provider answer shape. A valid caller answer is rejected or reaches the provider as the wrong scalar/array/option casing. The basic answer case uses canonical casing/array shapes and cannot catch these accepted compatibility forms. Oracle: Literal mysql/Auth/none output map independent of encoder implementation.

tests.name: answer_question refusals: unanswered question, invalid selection without custom, secret with attachments, unknown key, wrong requestId, none pending
tests.reason: Incomplete/invalid/unknown/secret-file/wrong-request answers are refused before any answer POST, with actionable reason. The tool partially answers a request, attaches a file to a secret or silently ignores an unknown key. Positive normalization does not exercise refusal/atomicity; upload-specific cases separately protect file batches. Oracle: Specific INVALID_ARGUMENT code plus missing question/allowed option/request ID evidence and zero POSTs.

tests.name: dismiss_question only for message-mode questions; resolve_approval validates the decision
tests.reason: Only dismissible async questions may be dismissed and approvals may use only the offered decision. Blocking user input is discarded or an unoffered permanent approval is sent. Answer submission cannot exercise dismissal or approval decision restrictions. Oracle: Literal dismiss request ID/route, offered accept/decline set and explicit INVALID_ARGUMENT/interrupt guidance for blocking dismissal.

tests.name: answer_question validates every question before uploading any attachment
tests.reason: Every question answer is validated before any attachment upload. A valid first answer uploads a file even though a later question remains unanswered. Bad-file batch validation cannot catch a missing answer before upload begins. Oracle: A two-question request with one missing answer, zero uploaded attachments and zero answer POSTs.

tests.name: answer_question keys: an exact id beats a 1-based index, and a question named twice is refused
tests.reason: Exact numeric question IDs take precedence over index aliases; duplicate aliases for one question are refused. An answer binds to another question because a numeric ID is interpreted as an index, or one answer silently overwrites another. Ordinary textual IDs/indexes do not create this ambiguity. Oracle: Independent numeric ID versus ordinal fixture, literal expected normalized key map and duplicate-name refusal.

tests.name: answer_question reports every problem at once, treats blank answers as unanswered, dedupes selections and takes files only where the GUI offers them
tests.reason: All answer problems are reported together, blanks remain unanswered, choices deduplicate and option-only questions reject files. The caller fixes one hidden error per retry, submits blank required fields or attaches unsupported content. Single-error refusal and normal answers do not prove aggregate reporting, blank handling or deduplication. Oracle: Literal simultaneous question/option/unknown-key diagnostics, repeated choices reducing to one and no upload/POST for forbidden files.

tests.name: answer_question: a blank answer beside files is normalized to an attachment-only answer
tests.reason: Files alone answer an allowed custom nonsecret question, with a normalized empty text answer and per-question references. An attachment-only answer is treated as missing or the provider never receives its uploaded file reference. Ordinary text/file batch cases require text and cannot catch the attachment-only exception. Oracle: Whitespace-only input becomes literal empty string; independently returned uploaded reference is under the literal question ID.

tests.name: resolve_approval lists every pending id when several are open, and resolves the one requested
tests.reason: Ambiguous pending approvals require explicit requestId; a selected approval resolves exactly its offered decision. A tool approves an arbitrary request when several are pending or approves the wrong request ID. One-request approval validation cannot reveal ambiguous-target selection. Oracle: Two literal pending IDs in refusal, selected r2 and expected acceptForSession body on the approval route.

tests.name: answer_question answers a Codex async question (responseMode "message") that outlived its turn: one /answer, the host makes it a message
tests.reason: A Codex async question that outlived its turn is still answered with exactly one answer command; the host owns converting it into a message. The tool starts another user turn itself or rejects a still-pending async question as stale. Blocking question cases do not exercise message-mode questions retained after turn completion. Oracle: Settled-turn/pending async fixture, exactly one /answer with request ID and normalized answers, no separate message route.

tests.name: a refusal quotes the caller's text cut short, so the tail that helps — Options, Questions, Pending — always survives the 4 000 cap
tests.reason: Refusals bound quoted untrusted caller values so allowed options/questions/pending IDs survive the 4000-character error cap. A huge invalid answer fills the refusal and hides the corrective choices, forcing blind retries. Normal-size error cases cannot catch clipping of useful tails by the executor error cap. Oracle: Oversize literal caller values and explicit retained Options/Questions/Pending tails with bounded safe error length and no POST.

tests.name: an empty requestId is refused, never read as omitted: with one request pending it would have acted on that one
tests.reason: Explicit empty requestId is invalid for answers/dismissal/approval and must never act as omission on a sole pending request. An empty ID unintentionally answers or approves the only request. Wrong nonempty IDs and ambiguous multiple requests do not exercise falsy-versus-omitted selection. Oracle: Empty-string schema/run refusals, specific INVALID_ARGUMENT and no POST despite an otherwise actionable single request.

tests.name: answer_question validates every file of every question before uploading any, and slices the refs back per question
tests.reason: All files across all questions are validated before any upload, then references return grouped by the original question and file order. A later invalid file leaves earlier uploads behind or valid files are attached to another question. Question completeness preflight cannot detect file-validation atomicity or flatten/slice grouping mistakes. Oracle: Invalid second-question file leaves zero upload/answer effects; positive fixture uses independently named refs and explicit expected grouped order.

tests.name: answer_question: a host refusal while uploading names the question and that question's own attachment index
tests.reason: A host upload refusal identifies the owning question and its local attachment index, and no later file or answer is sent. A flat upload index misdirects the caller to the wrong file or an answer is posted despite upload failure. Preflight bad-file cases never exercise a host failure after uploads begin or flat-to-local index translation. Oracle: Deliberate backend refusal at the second question, literal expected question/local index and observed bounded upload/zero answer effects.

tests.name: respond_to_request takes exactly one of answers, dismiss and decision; attachments only beside answers
tests.reason: respond_to_request accepts exactly one response action; attachments require answers. A mixed action ambiguously approves/dismisses/answers or performs backend work before rejecting invalid arguments. Each valid action/refusal case still supplies one action and cannot catch ambiguous top-level dispatch. Oracle: Concrete empty/mixed action payloads and attachments-without-answers rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT before any API calls.

tests.name: from a chat: add a per-project prompt (the chat's project by default) and a global one — Act, no card, createdBy stamped by the daemon
tests.reason: Chat create defaults to project or explicit global, runs as Act without card, and daemon stamps createdBy from trusted principal. Real persisted owner and project scope detect spoofed attribution/wrong default; lower service CRUD cannot see MCP principal propagation.

tests.name: create: project and global are exclusive; external callers name one; chats cannot pin; an external pin of an agent prompt is refused
tests.reason: Project/global selection is exclusive, external create must specify scope, chats cannot pin and external callers cannot pin agent-created prompts. Refusal codes plus actual untouched values catch forbidden pin/scope changes; creation happy path does not protect malformed inputs.

tests.name: an agent-created prompt no workflow uses: update and delete are Act, with no card
tests.reason: An unreferenced agent-created prompt permits Act update/delete without cards. Literal stored body/deleted identity and card count catch accidental Admin escalation; user/workflow-owned cases intentionally use different tier.

tests.name: the user's prompt: Admin saved-prompts — a card with the diff; grantable for this chat in Full access only, and the grant covers the next edit
tests.reason: Surviving public diff owner: user prompt edit requires saved-prompts Admin approval showing both distant removed/added body changes, writes approved text, offers grant only in Full access, and subsequent edit consumes grant. Real card/store/action outputs catch hidden changes or approval bypass. It now absorbs direct private unifiedDiff helper coverage without fixing hunk/context formatting. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: a prompt a workflow uses: Admin workflows — the card names the workflows, never a grant, even under a saved-prompts grant
tests.reason: Workflow-used prompt selects workflows Admin family, names actual referencing workflows, remains ungrantable even with saved-prompts grant, and workflow-owned caller cannot mutate. Real reference index and stored body catch family/grant bypass; user-created unreferenced ownership is different.

tests.name: fail closed: a prompt a workflow definition the daemon cannot read mentions counts as used — Admin workflows, never grantable, the card says why
tests.reason: Unreadable workflow mentioning prompt counts as use and requires ungrantable workflows Admin while unrelated prompt remains Act. Real index unreadable records and card outcomes detect fail-open unknown references; normal readable references cannot prove the failure path.

tests.name: what is approved is what runs: a prompt edited while its card waits is PREVIEW_STALE; one a workflow started using is refused
tests.reason: Prompt revision or newly started workflow use while card waits invalidates the operation before persistence. Deterministic approval callback changes independent store/reference data; PREVIEW_STALE/PERMISSION_DENIED and unchanged target catch approving stale content/authority.

tests.name: update/delete find the prompt among the global ones and the named (or own) project's; another workspace's user prompt is a cross-project card
tests.reason: Update/delete locate global and named/own-project prompts with proper cross-workspace user approval, never allowing chat pin or planning mutation. Distinct global identity and named project fixture catch looking only in current folder or granting wrong boundary access.

tests.name: list_saved_prompts: the chat's project and the global prompts, with createdBy and usedByWorkflows; bodies on request; query
tests.reason: List returns project+global rows, trusted creator/reference metadata, optional bodies and query results with below-Full cross-workspace reduction. Literal prompt ids/tags/bodies/reference fixtures detect incorrect scope/filter/projection; mutation approval tests cannot protect read privacy or optional body delivery.

tests.name: ruling S13: workflows of another workspace reach a chat below Full access only as a count; the user's card still names them
tests.reason: S13 hides other-workspace workflow names from below-Full agent results but human approval card still names them; Full access sees names. Literal sensitive workflow name presence/count is independent privacy oracle; ordinary list visibility does not test human-vs-agent distinction.

tests.name: repository prompts: the gate judges a prompt by its first checkout — a sibling checkout below Full access gets the same-workspace card, none at Full access
tests.reason: Shared repository prompt is judged by its original checkout, so sibling checkout needs same-workspace approval below Full and none at Full. Real repository origin fixtures catch using shared repoKey to bypass project gate; plain cross-project lookup does not exercise canonical owner. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: an agent that rewrote its origin to another repository gets no card-free access: hidden rows, cards for every edit, createdBy reduced
tests.reason: Rewritten repository origin cannot turn another checkout into own-scope card-free access: list hides rows, writes card, creator metadata reduces. Actual origin changes and literal hidden prompt/creator data detect trust in attacker-editable git config; ordinary static shared origin case cannot. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: a first checkout that no longer exists: an ungrantable boundary card naming it, in every mode; a checkout deleted while the card waits is PREVIEW_STALE
tests.reason: Missing original checkout requires ungrantable unknown-boundary approval in every mode; disappearing checkout during approval makes PREVIEW_STALE. Real directory removal and stored body verify filesystem identity remains stable; valid-checkout scope cases do not cover unavailable owner. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: a stale stored key: list_saved_prompts still lists the prompt in its own folder
tests.reason: A stale stored repository key must not hide a prompt from its own project folder. Persisted known prompt identity under changed remote catches lookup depending entirely on stale cache key; ordinary sibling repository sharing tests do not protect own-folder recovery.

tests.name: a workflow whose workspace is unknown (its project is no workspace's) reaches a chat below Full access only as a count — list rows and the update's result
tests.reason: Workflow project outside every workspace is unknown and below-Full agent receives only a count, both list and mutation result. Literal secret workflow title absence/count catch metadata leakage via unmapped workspace; named other-workspace cases cannot exercise unknown classification.

tests.name: expectWorkflowUses: a workflow that starts using the prompt between the tool's check and the store's write refuses the write — PREVIEW_STALE, nothing changed
tests.reason: Workflow use added after tool precheck but before actual store write must refuse update/delete with PREVIEW_STALE and leave stored prompt unchanged; direct rail-user operation remains allowed. Deterministic real reference/store interleaving catches the final TOCTOU window not covered by change while card waits.

tests.name: list_saved_prompts rows say usesUnknown when the index cannot tell; a global prompt's agent record without a thread is reduced below Full access
tests.reason: Unreadable index sets usesUnknown; threadless/future creator records loaded from persisted JSON redact below Full and remain meaningful at Full. Replace private library.prompts Map cast/mutation with valid persisted file plus public load(). Literal future schema records and caller results now test compatibility/privacy through stable storage boundary.

tests.name: search_sessions keeps only the hits of chat sessions open now, in the host's order, titled as list_sessions titles them
tests.reason: Search returns only currently open structured chats, preserves backend relevance order, uses live titles and honest turn/null/truncation metadata. Results point at closed/terminal tabs or reorder relevance by timestamps, invent a turn or miscount truncation. The host index cannot know current daemon tabs/titles; this is uniquely the MCP joining/projection boundary. Oracle: Literal mixed hit/open-session fixtures and independently expected c1/c2 result list, live titles, turn2/null and host truncated flag.

tests.name: role is only on a message hit and activityKind only on an activity hit
tests.reason: Message hits expose role only; activity hits expose activityKind only; absent fields are omitted rather than fabricated. A caller interprets an activity as a message because incompatible discriminator fields leak from index data. The ordinary mixed hits case contains no contradictory fields and cannot catch leaking invalid union fields. Oracle: Contradictory literal backend role/activityKind combinations and exact expected presence booleans per union arm.

tests.name: indexed:false is a normal answer: no hits and a hint that search is unavailable on this host right now
tests.reason: Unavailable/unindexed search is a normal honest empty response with guidance, including a missing backend response body. An unavailable index crashes or is presented as a complete successful no-match answer. Normal indexed hits cannot reveal unavailable-index handling. Oracle: indexed:false and absent-body fixtures, expected indexed/empty hits and unavailable hint; no session-list request.

tests.name: the trimmed query, the limit and the resolved project path reach the search route; the sessions read is the project's
tests.reason: Trimmed query, canonical project and limit route to search and session listing; omitted project searches globally and schema defaults/max remain public. A project-scoped search leaks another project or silently ignores limit/normalization. Backend index filtering tests do not exercise MCP project resolution/query forwarding or public input defaults. Oracle: Real temporary project resolution, literal expected queries/default20/max50 and global omission.

tests.name: a blank or over-long query and an unknown project are refused before anything is searched; the longest query is sent whole
tests.reason: Invalid blank/overlong Unicode queries and unknown/empty project are refused before search; maximum-length Unicode is accepted unchanged. UTF-16 counts incorrectly reject valid emoji queries or oversized/blank queries reach the host; invalid scope broadens globally. ASCII positive queries and limit tests cannot catch codepoint bounds or invalid-scope acceptance. Oracle: Concrete BMP/emoji/lone-surrogate/large inputs at independently owned 200-codepoint limit and zero search calls for invalid inputs.

tests.name: a result over the byte cap keeps the best hits: titles and snippets capped, the lowest-ranked dropped from the end
tests.reason: Large CJK search results fit the 60000-byte JSON budget, keep an ordered whole-hit prefix, report omitted count and cap snippets/titles without losing match markers. Byte accounting based on characters overflows multibyte result payloads or truncation drops higher-ranked hits/metadata. Generic result truncation destroys fields; ordinary small search cases cannot reveal projection-specific whole-hit fitting. Oracle: Independent JSON byte count, original ranked IDs, exact omitted arithmetic and marker-preserving bounded fixture fields.

tests.name: a failed search goes through daemonError: the host's code passes through, a crash's text never does
tests.reason: Typed host-unavailable failures survive; raw filesystem/SQLite failures become sanitized INTERNAL errors. A tool leaks daemon index paths or hides retryable host handover behind a generic failure. Successful/unindexed results have no thrown error, so cannot protect this privacy/failure boundary. Oracle: Literal HOST_UNAVAILABLE and raw ENOENT/private index path fixtures, expected safe code and absent path.

tests.name: secret_files_status for the chat's own project: files, every clone's states, and its own compare by name only
tests.reason: Secret status must show only metadata/key-name changes and clone states for the chat own project, never planted content/value fields accidentally supplied by the backend; synced files must not be compared.

tests.name: secret_files_status for a named project: an external caller names it (required) and gets that clone's compare
tests.reason: External secret-status callers must explicitly name a project, and the named clone must determine current/compare state instead of an unrelated clone.

tests.name: secret_files_status with no vault, no repo, or the plugin off: says so
tests.reason: No-vault/no-repository/plugin-disabled states must remain distinguishable while preserving useful existing metadata and refusing to suggest synchronization is active.

tests.name: push_secret_files is chat-only: an external caller has no such tool
tests.reason: The mutating secret push tool must be absent for external callers, rather than permitting remote API clients to bypass a chat approval card.

tests.name: push_secret_files is refused before any card: no project, no repo, no vault, nothing modified, an unmanaged path, the plugin off
tests.reason: Invalid/unmanaged/unavailable/nonmodified push requests must fail before any approval card or push request, with the correct independently specified refusal code.

tests.name: push_secret_files: the card names the repo, the source clone, each file's variable names and the clones overwritten — never a value, never a grant
tests.reason: Secret push approval must show source/repository/file/key names and overwritten/flagged clones without any values/tokens or reusable grant; approval must submit exactly those files/pinned tokens as the calling agent principal and report the normalized result. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: push_secret_files: named files push only the modified ones; the rest are reported, not pushed
tests.reason: An explicit file selection must push only selected modified files, reporting selected already-synced files without silently including other modified files.

tests.name: push_secret_files: a denied card pushes nothing
tests.reason: Denied secret approval must produce APPROVAL_DENIED and make zero push requests.

tests.name: push_secret_files: a file that changed while the card waited is PREVIEW_STALE, and nothing is pushed
tests.reason: A changed compare or changed vault version while approval waits must invalidate the preview before any push, preventing approval of a different secret update.

tests.name: push_secret_files: a copy whose content changed after the card (same variable names) is PREVIEW_STALE
tests.reason: A same-key value edit must still invalidate the preview through its content token, even though the variable-name compare is unchanged.

tests.name: push_secret_files: content changed between the run's re-read and the push is CONTENT_CHANGED, nothing pushed
tests.reason: If bytes change after preview re-read, the public request must carry the approved expect tokens and preserve CONTENT_CHANGED from the daemon. The fake backend checks expect only to expose the caller-visible race; it does not prove daemon disk atomicity.

tests.name: push_secret_files: never while planning, never for a workflow-owned chat
tests.reason: Planning/workflow-owned chats must be unable to perform Admin secret pushes and must open no approval card.

tests.name: asks as the calling chat and returns the value to this call
tests.reason: Only the calling chat may ask for the secret; the real structured value must be returned to that call and marked for host masking without copied note constants.

tests.name: every other outcome carries the record and no value
tests.reason: Dismissal/cancel/unavailable secret outcomes must expose their record but never a secret value.

tests.name: refuses arguments it does not know, and an empty prompt
tests.reason: Unknown input fields and empty secret prompts must fail INVALID_ARGUMENT before asking the user.

tests.name: answers UNAVAILABLE where the daemon wires no secret requests, and a cancelled call never asks
tests.reason: An unwired request service must report UNAVAILABLE and an already-aborted call must not prompt at all.

tests.name: works while planning and for a workflow-owned chat (no approval card involved); never for an external caller
tests.reason: Secrets must remain usable while planning/workflow-owned without Admin approval, and external clients must never access the chat-only tool.

tests.name: list_sessions: this chat's project by default, self marked; a terminal listed; nothing else
tests.reason: Chat list defaults own project, marks self and includes terminal only there; external list default includes all and cannot detect authority narrowing.
