tests.reason: Chat all below Full access narrows workspace plus own children, strips foreign goal content by mode, counts excluded projects and issues no broad approval card; full mode permits all.

tests.name: list_sessions of another workspace's project: a cross-workspace-read card below Full access (S13), none in it
tests.reason: Explicit other-workspace metadata list must request cross-workspace-read approval except Full access; narrowed all intentionally never cards unknown fanout. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.reason: Other-project metadata get below content rights strips reply/goal/queued-preview without content card, while auto permits marked untrusted content; secret words cannot leak through metadata.

tests.name: get_session: lineage, a delegate's settled reply as its result, and the caller itself
tests.reason: Delegate settled reply must move to result with lineage/threadRef relationship, while self gets no untrusted notice and its own child links; ordinary external detail does not transform delegate result.

tests.name: get_session of another workspace below Full access: a metadata card (S13); content still omitted after approval

tests.reason: Content transcript read in other project below auto must require target-named boundary card; own project/auto remain free. Executor policy plus actual tool classification is asserted. tests.name: search_sessions: own project by default; "all" narrowed per mode and never carded; a named other project follows the matrix
tests.reason: Search defaults own scope; all narrows by runtime mode without cards, with accurate excluded projects; explicit foreign project follows approval matrix and result has untrusted notice.

tests.name: control_session: interrupt any chat but self; stop_process/compact/rewind/close only on agent-created children (§13 c)
tests.reason: Chat controls may interrupt sibling but not self; destructive controls require agent-created children, GUI fork is user-owned, and missing rewind count refuses. Exact successful writes prove authority gate not just error shape.

tests.name: control_session while planning: a data change is refused, stopping work is not
tests.reason: Planning caller cannot compact data but may interrupt work; real writes show only allowed interruption reaches daemon.

tests.name: control_session on an own child in another workspace: a cross-project Act card below Full access
tests.reason: Own-created child in another workspace still needs cross-project Act approval below Full access; lineage ownership does not erase project boundary. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: update_session: own title yes, own settings no; children only; never a broader mode
tests.reason: Self title only, children settings only, never broader permission mode; unknown caller mode fails closed and planning blocks writes. Successful title control distinguishes blanket refusal.

tests.name: respond_to_request: own children's provider questions only; never a decision, a secret, or an Orquester card
tests.reason: Chat respond only accepts own child's nonsecret provider question, never decision/other chat/GUI fork/Orquester card; no write precedes refusal and real allowed answer reaches correct route.

tests.name: respond_to_request's boundary card lists an inline attachment by name and size, never its bytes
tests.reason: Boundary preview for inline attachment must show filename/3000-byte size and answer but never encoded bytes; approval UI must not disclose hidden file payload.

tests.name: a workflow-owned caller's "all" is narrowed too, and a would-be card is a denial
tests.reason: Workflow-owned caller all remains narrowed and would-be content card becomes denial with no approval; unattended workflow cannot request authority interactively.

tests.name: §4.3: another chat's words are marked — list rows with goal text, and the session detail an Act returns
tests.reason: Another chat's returned words require leading untrusted notice across list/control/update/respond; own text and no-content close omit notice. This cross-tool injection boundary differs from view shaping.

tests.name: the chat frame is measured: a 200-character CJK title cannot push get_turn_diff or read_tool_output past the result cap

tests.name: external callers through the executor: respond_to_request takes a decision; control_session argument errors come from scope, before any read

tests.reason: External list kind/project/attention filters must return fixed tab IDs/order and real project query; chat caller authorization narrowing is a separate executor seam.

tests.name: no session tool reads an empty string as omitted: an empty project, agent, model or cwd is refused, never a default
tests.reason: Empty project/agent/model/cwd/account must refuse instead of selecting defaults, with no mutation; field-specific schema issue paths diagnose actual validation boundary.

tests.name: get_session returns a detail for a chat and a view for a terminal; unknown id errors
tests.reason: Actual get_session dispatch must choose chat detail vs terminal view and reject unknown ID; pure views cannot detect wrong tool branch/lookup.

tests.name: create_session validates everything up front and posts the GUI's body (claude, then a resume)
tests.reason: Creation must serialize real GUI launch fields and resolve saved conversation account/title/resume metadata before POST; fake create response does not build requested body.

tests.name: create_session profile (Agent Profiles §5.5): by id or case-insensitive name, sent as profileId on an unattended launch; omitted = Global
tests.reason: Profile case-insensitive name/id must resolve correct profileId on unattended body, while omitted stays Global; result echoes cannot hide wrong POST fields.

tests.name: create_session profile refusals: unknown → PROFILE_NOT_FOUND before any create; not ready / unsupported → the daemon's refusal naming the profile, never Global
tests.reason: Unknown/unavailable/not-ready/unsupported profiles must preserve correct refusal and never fall back Global; fake failures isolate backend, tool resolves/annotates profile context.

tests.name: get_session and list_sessions report each chat's Agent Profile ({id, name}, or null for Global); list_agents lists the profiles with per-agent readiness
tests.reason: Get/list/list_agents must wire profile names/readiness/reasons, preserve Global null, and tolerate old daemon without profile endpoint; pure profile ref tests cannot prove tool context loading.

tests.name: create_session resume: a system-home row never forces System, a mismatched agent is refused
tests.reason: System transcript resume must allow account default or explicit system, while mismatched agent must refuse without POST; account-home ownership matters for resume identity.

tests.name: create_session cwd: resolved against the project, and it must be an existing directory inside the sandbox
tests.reason: Real temp cwd resolution accepts existing project directory absolute/relative, rejects missing/file/escape before POST; filesystem sandbox boundary is exercised rather than mocked.

tests.name: create_session refusals: unknown project, disabled agent, bad model, wrong-family account, cwd escape, unknown conversation, session cap
tests.reason: Unknown project/model/account/conversation and24-running-session cap must refuse without create; title also claims disabled-agent/cwd cases not executed here (cwd owned separately).

tests.name: create_session: a read that fails after the create names the created session, so a retry does not open a second one
tests.reason: Post-create detail failure must preserve created sessionId/created:true and underlying safe code, never retry create or expose host socket path; prevents duplicate tabs on caller retry.

tests.name: create_session: a failed read's own detail can never hide which tab was created — sessionId and created:true win a key clash
tests.reason: Backend error detail with colliding sessionId/created fields must not override actual created tab identity; generic merge behavior otherwise misleads recovery.

tests.name: update_session: one /mode body for model+effort+runtimeMode, rename via PUT, account via /account, no-ops skipped
tests.reason: Rename/mode/account writes must carry exact bodies, merge model/options atomically, skip system-account no-op and report only applied changes; fake records requests without implementing transformation.

tests.name: update_session gates: busy without force, idle gate for accounts, opencode has no account, wrong family
tests.reason: REWRITE finding: OpenCode-specific refusal currently false-positive because OpenCode is absent from registry and acc-1 wrong family; removing dedicated guard still INVALID_ARGUMENT. Use known enabled OpenCode registry/catalog + accountId=system so missing guard succeeds. Busy/force/wrong-family subcases remain legitimate.

tests.name: update_session during a turn: a call whose every field already holds its value is a no-op, not SESSION_BUSY
tests.reason: All equal values mid-turn must return no applied writes rather than busy/restart; a genuinely changed option still refuses. No-op detection protects active work.

tests.name: update_session: an options-only change keeps the head's model and merges onto the head's options
tests.reason: Options-only change must preserve nondefault opus and unrelated thinking option while replacing effort, with one mode command; recreating default selection would silently switch model.

tests.name: update_session: an account switch while a goal continues is refused with the host's advice before anything is written — mid-turn and between the goal's turns
tests.reason: Continuing active goal forbids account switch both mid-turn/between turns, before even rename/forced mode write; paused goal permits carry. Atomic prevalidation protects identity/work.

tests.name: update_session: a summary still saying continuing after the goal was paused loses to the thread just read — the host needs an active goal to continue it
tests.reason: Fresh paused/cleared snapshot overrides stale continuing summary for account switch; actual running turn still enforces busy. Metadata lag must not permanently block operations.

tests.name: update_session: a goal an Orquester update holds refuses the switch with its own advice before anything is written; mid-turn, a mode change is told to wait
tests.reason: Deploy-held paused/continuing goal blocks account switch before writes, while its final running turn retains ordinary busy gate; user-paused goal has different restart semantics.

tests.name: update_session: a rename needs no catalogue entry; a write that fails mid-way reports only what landed
tests.reason: Rename must work for retired agent without catalogue; later mode refusal must preserve applied=['title'] so partial successful write is caller-visible.

tests.name: interrupt_session names the running turn, and with none stops the background work; stop_session posts session/stop
tests.reason: Interrupt must use current head turn t3, not stale summary t2; no active turn sends empty body to stop fleet, and stop_process uses session/stop.

tests.name: stop_task posts task/stop with the task id, and passes the host's refusal through
tests.reason: Task stop must dispatch exact taskId/seq, propagate workflow refusal, and reject terminal before POST; ordinary session stop cannot protect task targeting.

tests.name: close_session sends the DELETE for the tab it names, chat or terminal, and refuses an unknown id without sending one
tests.reason: Close chat/terminal must DELETE actual named IDs and return closed; unknown/refused close must never falsely report success or send unknown deletion.

tests.name: compact_session posts exactly the compact command, returns its seq with the session, and passes a host refusal through
tests.reason: Compact must send only compact command, return receipt/detail, reject terminal and propagate unavailable cause; inbound compacted state tests do not own outbound command.

tests.name: revert_session returns the settled turn count and accepted command receipt
tests.reason: Accepted rewind must POST targetTurnCount1 and return seq8 plus settled detailcount1; fake state transition doesn't construct command or choose completion.

tests.name: revert_session does not lose a session event delivered during its read
tests.reason: A session event arriving during snapshot read must wake/re-read and observe count0; subscribing after the read loses this race and hangs.

tests.name: revert_session ignores stale failure rows and reports a new adapter refusal
tests.reason: Rewind wait must ignore preexisting failure IDs but report newly added refusal with seq/activityId/cause; old failures cannot answer a new accepted command.

tests.name: revert_session reaches its ten-second deadline without reposting the command
tests.reason: Controlled10-second deadline must reject SESSION_BUSY with receipt and issue exactly one POST; silent retry could repeat destructive rewind.

tests.name: revert_session wakes on a session update while the clock is held
tests.reason: A relevant bus update must complete rewind while virtual time does not advance; sleep/poll-only implementation would hang despite completed operation.

tests.name: revert_session aborts a paused wait without another daemon read
tests.reason: Abort must terminate parked rewind with receipt without another daemon read; cancelled callers must release resources immediately.

tests.name: revert_session reports a session closed during its wait with the receipt
tests.reason: Session closure during rewind must reject SESSION_NOT_FOUND with accepted seq; timeout/busy failure would conceal lost target identity.

tests.name: revert_session: a failure after the POST keeps its code and message and gains the seq — in the wait, and reading the detail after it
tests.reason: Post-acceptance read failures must retain safe code/message, merge own seq over foreign seq, and redact thrown socket path in both wait and final detail stages.

tests.name: revert_session refuses up front a target before the last settled compaction — the GUI's rule — and nothing is posted
tests.reason: Rewind before last settled compaction must refuse without POST; allowed boundary retains correct turn count. Real transcript markers define lost context, not incidental item positions.

tests.name: revert_session places a turn with no user message by its first row, and one with no row left by its own start
tests.reason: Promptless/retained-without-rows turns must still locate compaction boundary by first row or start timestamp; valid cut remains allowed and unresolvable earlier cut refuses.

tests.name: revert_session refuses while a request is open (PENDING_REQUEST, like send_message), a turn is active (SESSION_BUSY), rollback is missing or the count is out of range
tests.reason: Pending/native or message-mode cards, active turn, missing rollback capability, out-of-range count and fresh empty chat must all refuse before POST; each prevents invalid destructive rewind.

tests.name: interrupt_session and the busy gates read the thread head, not only the (lagging) summary
tests.reason: Fresh running head must override lagging ready summary for interrupt and update/rewind busy gates; summary-only tests cannot catch stale-state authority decisions.

tests.name: get_turn_diff defaults to the latest checkpointed turn, includes the checkpoint files and bounds the diff to the result budget
tests.reason: Diff defaults to actual latest checkpoint, preserves files/query whitespace option, truncates JSON/UTF8-heavy data within60000, keeps small diff and propagates missing checkpoint error.

tests.name: get_turn_diff: a small diff leaves its room to the file list — a 400-file rename is listed whole
tests.reason: Small diff leaves budget for400-file full list; larger list preserves ordered prefix/accurate omitted count while diff stays whole. Overtrimming files to a fixed share loses real data.

tests.name: get_turn_diff with no turn named and no checkpoint yet refuses on its own, before asking the host for a diff
tests.reason: No checkpoint/default turn must refuse locally before requesting /diff; backend404 alone would obscure unavailable operation and waste work.

tests.name: get_turn_diff bounds a huge file list too: the head that fits, filesTruncated and omittedFiles, and the diff keeps the rest of the budget
tests.reason: Large diff plus5000-file list must fit cap with ordered prefix, accurate omitted flags/count and nonempty diff; small-diff budget owner exercises different allocation pressure.

tests.name: spec §11: get_session_lineage is get_session's lineage and pending deliveries; the external surface names the unified tools only
tests.reason: Lineage/pending deliveries must be returned through unified get_session; external catalog must exclude deprecated tool names and retain named public tools per §11. This is public MCP discovery compatibility, not private export inventory.

tests.name: control_session refuses arguments of another action, and an action missing its own
tests.reason: Cross-action/missing required control args must return INVALID_ARGUMENT with no POST; a permissive schema alone cannot protect semantic action-field exclusivity.

tests.name: a project list is keyed by the project path, whichever spelling of the project is given
tests.reason: Surviving project-address owner: name/path spellings must resolve one stored project list and serialized results must omit internal refKey. Literal expected absolute project path and result identities detect wrong scope/storage key or leaking internals. Now absorbs the lower create/list mapping scenarios, so their second real-server startups add no protection.

tests.name: external callers pass exactly one of workspace or project, and the project must resolve inside the sandbox
tests.reason: External selectors are exclusive/required and sandbox resolution refuses escaping/missing paths before write. Literal refusal codes and empty store catch access outside configured filesystem; lower helper-name tests protect distinct helper inputs, not executor mutual-exclusion/default rules.

tests.name: each action takes its own fields: a missing one or a stray one is INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is written
tests.reason: Each action requires its own fields and rejects forbidden/stray fields before persistence. A literal invalid request matrix with actual untouched store catches silent partial mutations from malformed public catalog inputs; lower route validation only covers toggle HTTP payloads.

tests.name: update renames and replaces the body; toggle ticks one item; delete removes the list
tests.reason: Single real-executor/InjectDaemonApi/real-store lifecycle owner for create/update/toggle/delete. Literal independent body bytes now include prose, dash/star task markers, stored whitespace, uppercase X, index selection and lowercase text lookup. Detects incorrect index/text matching, mutation of unrelated bytes, loss of no-op preservation, misrouted action or failed persistence; removed facade scenarios cannot add a distinct outcome.

tests.name: list_todos keeps one result: the oldest lists are left out first, and the result says so and how many
tests.reason: Result-budget overflow keeps newest lists, reports omitted oldest and returns one valid capped result. Literal ordering and independent UTF8 JSON size catch losing newest data or overflowing tool transport; ordinary small CRUD cannot protect this budget policy.

tests.name: list_todos: a newest list too big for a result on its own keeps its name and the head of its body, marked bodyTruncated
tests.reason: A single oversized newest list keeps name plus body prefix and advertises bodyTruncated. Literal prefix, size and flags catch silently claiming partial data is whole; multi-list dropping case does not protect an individually oversized row.

tests.name: toggle on a 3 000-item list: the toggle is whole, its result one result marked bodyTruncated; a same-state retry writes nothing
tests.reason: 3000-task toggle must update the full store, clip only returned body, and explicit same-state retry must cause no updated event; name-only rename preserves full body. Independent original task fixture/full expected body catches using clipped tool output as write source or idempotent duplicate writes.

tests.name: a name too long for any result is the one thing cut, never the id
tests.reason: An oversized name can be clipped in a response but id and stored name remain whole. Literal identity/full store value and UTF8 result budget catch unusable ids or destructive name clipping; oversized-body cases cannot exercise metadata dominating the cap.

tests.name: chat: without workspace or project a call is on this chat's project; its own lists are Act with no card
tests.reason: A chat without selectors operates on its own project, allowing its own read/write as Act without an approval. Actual store and card count expose wrong default target or accidental Admin card; external selectors cannot protect thread context.

tests.name: chat: another project of the workspace reads freely and acts behind a card below Full access
tests.reason: Another project in the same workspace reads freely; writes need approval below Full access and none in Full access, while denial leaves store unchanged. Real other-project data and approval outcomes catch wrong gate matrix cell; own-project and cross-workspace cases have different permissions.

tests.name: chat: another workspace's own lists (S13 workspace target) — a read below Full access is a card, a write always cards; never grantable
tests.reason: Other-workspace metadata reads require a card below Full access, writes card in every mode, grants unavailable, denied write unchanged and workflow-owned Act remains allowed. Replace swallowed failed empty-list toggle with real task and checked=true assertion. Literal outcomes now detect actual authorized mutation failures rather than passing an unrelated error. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: chat: writes are refused while planning; otherwise any chat may use them, nothing to turn on first
tests.reason: Planning refuses writes while permitting reads; otherwise agent kind/role/toolset does not disable these ordinary todo operations. Real data/no-card outcomes catch unnecessary availability gating or plan mutation; Admin workflow restrictions do not own this Act behavior.

tests.name: get_usage forwards the explicit refresh request; quota is the default and stays at the top level (parity)
tests.reason: Quota is the default include; explicit refresh alone maps to the quota query, external callers retain account emails and chat callers never receive them.

tests.name: get_usage cost windows the rows to the last N UTC days and totals them
tests.reason: Cost results must window real rows to the requested UTC days, preserve asOf and total only included costs without reading quota unnecessarily.

tests.name: get_usage cost rounds row costs, keeps an unpriced row's null and projects the row shape
tests.reason: Cost row projection must round monetary output, preserve unknown-price null and strip nonpublic/internal cost-breakdown fields rather than fabricating price.

tests.name: get_usage cost keeps an oversized result in budget by dropping the oldest days' rows, never the totals
tests.reason: Large cost data must fit its UTF8 JSON budget by dropping only whole oldest-day row groups, preserving exact full-window totals and honest dropped-row count.

tests.name: isoWeek: ISO 8601 weeks in UTC, the week-year of the Thursday, Monday as `from`
tests.reason: ISO 8601 defines January dates in the previous week-year and late-December dates in the next. Assert literal 2026-W53/2025-W01 buckets and Mondays through production-consumed costView aggregation; ordinary September weekly tests already own weekday grouping. This removes the test-only isoWeek export and helper-call coupling without losing either year-boundary regression.
tests.new_name: weekly cost uses the ISO week-year across December and January

tests.name: get_usage cost by week extends the window back to the Monday of its first week: no partial week (days 7 on Thursday 2026-10-15)
tests.reason: Weekly cost windows must include the entire first ISO week, whereas day windows must retain the exact day cutoff.

tests.name: get_usage cost by week: one row per agent, model and ISO week, priced when any day is; week totals with their Monday
tests.reason: Weekly aggregation must group by agent/model/week, sum token/cost values, retain unpriced rows as null and expose week totals with their Monday.

tests.name: get_usage cost counts Grok from Orquester's own chats (its reported cost), labelled Orquester chats only; an unreadable source says so
tests.reason: Grok costs must use reported Orquester chat settlements, subtract cached input correctly, preserve UTC windows and clearly disclose host-external usage exclusion or an unavailable source.

tests.name: get_usage session: sums the snapshot's turn tokens and prices Codex turns from the cost table (costSource estimated)
tests.reason: Session usage must aggregate settled/unknown-usage turns, separate cache/reasoning values and estimate Codex costs with the correct source tag; session-only requests must not read quota.

tests.name: get_usage session: a per-turn reported cost (OpenCode, Grok) wins; reported + estimated is mixed; a turn's own model prices it; unpriced and partial are said
tests.reason: Provider-reported costs must take precedence for Grok/OpenCode, mixed per-turn reported/estimated prices must sum correctly, turn-level models must price their own usage and partial/unpriced results must be disclosed.

tests.name: get_usage session: a Claude session is priced from its turns' own tokens, never by summing the CLI's cumulative total_cost_usd (fixtures 11, 12, 17, 19)
tests.reason: Claude session cost must derive from per-turn main-agent tokens, never sum process-cumulative cost frames across turns/resumes/subagents. Retain FIXTURE_11 and two-turn workflow oracles; remove FIRST_TURNS single-turn price repetitions already owned at the calculator fixture seam in usage-tokens.test.ts.

tests.name: get_usage session: a Claude alias slug is priced as the model the provider catalogue resolves it to
tests.reason: Provider-catalogue aliases must resolve to their supplied concrete model for pricing, while an unresolved alias must remain honestly unpriced instead of guessed.

tests.name: get_usage session: Codex cache-written tokens bill at the input price (its row has no cache-write rate), as the Cost tab counts them
tests.reason: Codex cache-created tokens must remain part of its input-price total when the model has no cache-write tariff; treating them as free would underreport cost.

tests.name: get_usage session needs a sessionId and a chat session; its scope is that session's metadata
tests.reason: Session-specific usage must require a valid chat session ID and claim only that session/project metadata; irrelevant sessionId arguments and nonexistent targets must be refused before approvals.

tests.name: get_usage session: a context-tagged model (claude-opus-4-8[1m]) is priced at its standard rates — fixture 01's catalogue: `default` and `opus[1m]`
tests.reason: Fails unique protection: context-tag tariff normalization is already asserted with the same captured fixture and exact unrounded charge in daemon usage-tokens.test.ts; the retained MCP Claude alias case independently owns provider-catalog resolution. This replays their composition with two incidental alias spellings and adds no transformation or failure branch.

tests.name: get_usage session: mainAgentOnly always, with the turns that ran subagents and the conversation's compactions counted (the estimate is a floor there)
tests.reason: Session estimates must always disclose main-agent scope, count turns that ran subagents and count only settled compactions, preserving absence of counts for plain sessions.
