tests.name: a user's own MCP server keeps its result as before (no session tool, no bounding)
tests.reason: An ordinary user-installed MCP server must retain its result/image payload unchanged; session-tool privacy scrubbing cannot corrupt unrelated integrations.

tests.name: `${name} refuses ${JSON.stringify(args).slice(0, 70)}`
tests.reason: Public viewport/HTML/title/height limits and unknown-thread inputs must refuse with INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field before any publish/preview.

tests.name: accepts the bounds themselves
tests.reason: Inclusive public argument boundaries must succeed through execution, preventing schemas from rejecting valid maximum/minimum requests.

tests.name: publishes into the CALLING chat and answers the reference and the message, as text and structured
tests.reason: A publication must target only the calling thread with source HTML/title/height/cancellation signal and expose its attachment reference consistently as JSON/text.

tests.name: answers a refusal as an error result with the publisher's own message
tests.reason: A deliberate publisher failure must become an error result preserving the safe reason/code.

tests.name: works while the chat plans, in every permission mode, and for a workflow-owned chat
tests.reason: Publishing must work for every permission mode, planning and workflow-owned chats without introducing a spurious approval boundary.

tests.name: is no external tool
tests.reason: External tool execution must refuse html_render so it cannot publish into an unrelated agent thread.

tests.name: answers the screenshot as MCP image content first (its own type), then the measurements as JSON
tests.reason: Preview must preserve screenshot bytes/MIME first as MCP image and expose returned measurements separately as structured/text data.

tests.name: leaves width and appearance to the daemon's defaults when the agent omits them
tests.reason: Omitted appearance/width must remain omitted at the daemon call so the real renderer controls its defaults; no geometry snapshot is frozen.

tests.name: answers no browser, a timeout, or a cancellation as an error result
tests.reason: Missing browser/timeout/cancel must expose their distinct deliberate outcomes, and an aborted call must not start a preview.

tests.name: wait_for_session returns flagged sessions after the cursor, newest first, with a new cursor
tests.reason: Waiting returns flagged sessions newer than the cursor, attention reasons, newest first, with advanced cursor and no timeout. An orchestrator misses work or repeats already processed sessions because cursor/reason/order are wrong. Lower-level event waits do not prove final MCP SessionView/reason/cursor projection. Oracle: Fixed attention instants and independent expected b/approval then a/completed with cursor stamp7.

tests.name: wait_for_session orders by the attention instant, newest first, a tie going to the newer tab
tests.reason: Attention ordering uses actual instants across timezone offsets and newer creation time breaks equal instants. A lexicographic timestamp sort puts an older offset instant first or destabilizes tied tabs. The ordinary UTC-only distinct-attention case cannot expose string sorting or tie breaking. Oracle: Literal offset timestamp with known earlier UTC instant and expected newer/older/offset IDs and stamp6 cursor.

tests.name: wait_for_session defaults `after` to now, honours session and project filters, and rejects both
tests.reason: Default after is now, event subscription precedes initial read, and session/project filters select only intended targets; conflicting/unknown selectors fail. A completion racing the initial read is missed until timeout or a project wait returns another project activity. Static ready-session tests cannot reveal the lost-event race or filter/default-now isolation; virtual time removes real timeout waits without changing assertions. Oracle: A deferred subscription/read barrier emits a concrete session.updated event, fixed/jumping clocks, real project fixture and explicit returned IDs/cursor/error codes.

tests.name: wait_for_session checks `after` before any lookup and never reads an empty id or project as absent
tests.reason: Invalid after is rejected before lookup; empty ID/project never means watch every session. A typo expands a scoped wait globally or unknown-session lookup masks an invalid cursor. Valid filters/conflicting selectors do not exercise empty/falsy expansion or precedence of cursor validation. Oracle: Literal yesterday/empty selectors with expected INVALID_ARGUMENT or PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, including invalid cursor plus unknown ID.

tests.name: create → run → fix → run → delete under ONE chat grant: the approved create makes the grant and joins it; nothing else cards
tests.reason: Real approval port/store creates a chat grant from approved create and joins that workflow; run→patch→run→enable→delete then use it with correct receipts and no further cards. Literal persisted membership, backend revision and run count catch broken executor/registry/store wiring that FakeApprovalPort cases cannot.

tests.name: a second create joins the chat's grant only through the card that says so; approve-once of another workflow's run never widens the grant
tests.reason: A second create joins the existing grant only through a card; approve-once of an unrelated workflow never expands it, while explicit grant choice does. Real membership/card/denial outcomes catch accidental authority growth. Replace constant-equality notice copy with a semantic grant warning.

tests.name: the grant never covers a change whose union leaves the caller's project, a caller below Full access, or a workflow secret
tests.reason: An existing grant cannot cover a cross-project union, caller below Full access or workflow secret. Actual card options and typed-secret fields prove real runtime scope. Remove the secret non-disclosure assertion over an empty resolved-approval list; the actual chat-secret test checks nonempty card/result data.

tests.name: no escape through sub-workflows: wiring the user's (disabled) workflow into a granted one, and running it, both card until that workflow is granted too
tests.reason: Wiring a disabled user workflow into a granted parent requires consent; approving once leaves only the parent covered, explicit grant adds the child and then permits parent runs. Real stored ids and backend frozen children catch subworkflow privilege escalation through the real registry.

tests.name: race: a workflow outside the grant that starts running this one between the grant's check and the write — PREVIEW_STALE, nothing saved or deleted
tests.reason: A new outside caller appearing after the grant check must cause the daemon expectCallers precondition to reject update/delete as PREVIEW_STALE, leaving name/revision/existence unchanged. A deterministic reference race catches missing final preconditions or wrong result mapping through the real port.

tests.name: list_workflow_block_types filters the requested block type
tests.reason: Filter supplied block-type records to the requested type and tolerate older daemon records without guide; catches wrong schema advertised for an agent block. Supplied catalog rows are independent daemon data, not the mapping oracle.

tests.name: list_workflow_block_types returns a type's guide sections only when that type is asked for
tests.reason: Return the requested type's supplied guide while omitting per-type guide bulk from the all-types answer; advertised authoring references must name live tool routes. Detects dropping authoring help or directing callers to removed tool names.

tests.name: list_workflow_block_types omits the largest schemas and identifies them
tests.reason: Over-budget block catalogs omit large schemas while retaining small ones and naming omitted types; catches blanket truncation that removes useful type identities or silently loses schemas.

tests.name: create_workflow maps named edges and project, requests layout, and defaults disabled in the host timezone
tests.reason: Public create fields map project address and named edges into daemon request, disabled default, automatic layout and host timezone. Literal request and response fields detect wrong persistence defaults, time interpretation or project target; engine creation tests cannot protect MCP translation.

tests.name: create_workflow passes temp targets through and refuses unknown projects or malformed arguments
tests.reason: Temporary project targets pass through, missing existing projects reject, and malformed/unknown fields fail public argument validation; catches unintended persistent definition under wrong scope or ignored caller typo.

tests.name: a block's type, position and retry values are left to the daemon's add, which refuses them clearly (create and update)
tests.reason: Unknown block types, invalid retry and positions must be refused through the shared patch/add validator in create/update dry runs with correct offending entry. Detects MCP falsely declaring an invalid definition valid before daemon save; independent block-type/schema contract supplies input constraints.

tests.name: create_workflow identifies refused edges and exposes daemon validation problems
tests.reason: Daemon refusal index must identify the corresponding user edge, and returned validation errors must retain independent severity/code counts. Detects unusable diagnostics referring to combined internal add indices or losing meaningful errors.

tests.name: create_workflow {dryRun: true} validates the definition the create would save and saves nothing (was validate_workflow)
tests.reason: Dry-run create validates the same complete definition and translated named connections that a save would use, reports independent error/warning problems and performs no create. Detects previews approving unvalidated graph or dry run mutating state.

tests.name: get_workflow selects a named block and incident edges and preserves missing-identity diagnostics
tests.reason: Named block read returns the correct node and only incident connections, whole workflow revision and actionable missing workflow/node diagnostics; catches wrong block selected or broken recovery tool identity.

tests.name: workflow reads and writes identify truncated long text while keeping short text whole
tests.reason: Large source fields in created/read workflows must be marked truncated and retain a prefix while short fields stay whole. Detects partial code returned as editable whole or unnecessary loss of small data; wide-outline case is a different multi-block overflow strategy.

tests.name: update_workflow preserves conflict hints and recovers a legacy failing-op index
tests.reason: 409 conflict retains re-read recovery and legacy failing-op message maps to caller op index/type, preserving explicit native index too. Detects wrong edit retry or misleading failure location across supported daemon response forms.

tests.name: update_workflow validates op shapes and resolves project fields (set_project, an update_node's projectOverride) before sending the batch
tests.reason: Invalid op shapes reject; set_project and per-node override resolve before sending one patch batch. Literal expected paths/ops catch an MCP write aimed outside resolved project or malformed forwarded patch; shared patcher tests do not see address translation.

tests.name: update_workflow {dryRun: true}: the local replay of the ops is validated, the changes listed, nothing saved
tests.reason: Dry-run patch replays sequential changes against revision, lists semantic changed fields, rejects stale or failing op and never patches. Detects evaluating wrong revision or mutating during validation; create dry-run cannot protect patch replay semantics.

tests.name: list_workflows resolves the project filter and maps the daemon's summaries
tests.reason: List project filter maps to actual projectPath query and daemon summary fields become caller workflow identity/triggers/active-run count; external no-filter lists all. Detects wrong project list or unusable run/workflow identifiers.

tests.name: run_workflow maps run/overlap answers, needs the revision, and sends input or force to the daemon
tests.reason: Run requires current revision, forwards expectedRevision/input/force and reports overlap skip truthfully; stale input must not start. Detects accidentally running newer definition or treating skipped overlap as a real run; engine tests do not protect MCP precondition/body mapping.

tests.name: run_workflow wait finishes on its event and returns block data in definition order
tests.reason: Run wait resolves on workflow completion event, returns definition-ordered block statuses/output/session/account hops/finalOutput and removes listener. Independent run record deliberately has shuffled blocks; detects misleading result or leaked subscription. Controlled time avoids waiting.

tests.name: run_workflow timeout returns the current run and releases its subscription
tests.reason: Expired run wait reports running snapshot with timedOut and removes listener, using virtual clock. Detects timeout hanging/leak or falsely claiming finished; event success cannot protect deadline path.

tests.name: run_workflow wait rereads a silently finished run and releases its subscription on abort
tests.reason: Periodic safety reread finds a silently finished run; abort completes cancelled/unfinished and releases listener. Detects event-loss hang and cancellation leaks separately from ordinary timeout/event success.

tests.name: get_workflow_runs {runId} fits outputs and {runId, nodeId} pages whole Unicode output without losing bytes (was get_workflow_run)
tests.reason: Run overview clips huge output but preserves truncation provenance; explicit per-node output pages reconstruct Unicode JSON exactly and small output remains value. Detects byte/codepoint cursor corruption or claiming clipped output whole; also protects missing node/run recovery.

tests.name: get_workflow_runs {workflowId} pages a workflow's runs (was list_workflow_runs); runId-only fields need a runId
tests.reason: Workflow-run listing forwards page cursor/limit and returns next cursor; run-only field combinations and excessive waits reject. Detects repeated/skipped history or interpreting node/log/watch fields without run identity.

tests.name: get_workflow_runs {runId, waitSeconds} waits on the bus for an active run to end (watch), and returns at once for an ended one
tests.reason: Watch an existing active run until event signals terminal snapshot; already-ended run returns immediately without subscriptions. Detects waiting on completed runs or failing to refresh event output, distinct from starting a run with wait.

tests.name: get_workflow_runs {runId, nodeId, log} reads a block's stdout/stderr: tail defaults, paging and approximate offsets for masked logs
tests.reason: Workflow debug API must tail stdout by default, honor explicit head offsets, keep stderr and block failure metadata, and mark masked-log offsets approximate. Backend fixture text and literal offsets/stream selection are independent; ordinary run-summary tests do not read block logs.

tests.name: delete_workflow needs confirm: true
tests.reason: Delete refuses absent/false confirm and returns target identity only after explicit true. Detects accidental destructive action without documented confirmation; chat approval is separate authorization layer.

tests.name: secrets are write-only and scoped; external callers set with value or delete; malformed or oversized secret inputs are refused
tests.reason: External secret writes/deletes route global/workflow scope correctly, never return supplied values and strip hostile value from listing; malformed name/oversize/mutually incompatible value-delete refuse. Literal leaked marker catches actual credential exposure, distinct from chat-typed flow.

tests.name: get_workflow maps workflow errors, bounds problem detail and hides internal failures
tests.reason: Workflow error envelopes preserve public conflict/validation codes, sort errors before bounded problem detail and conceal host failures. Independent HTTP responses and 150 problems catch security leakage or relevant errors dropped behind warnings.

tests.name: wide definitions retain every block identity in an outline and allow full per-block reads
tests.reason: Wide definitions outline every block id/type and allow full named-block recovery; catches identities disappearing under result cap or per-block reads remaining truncated. Different failure from one oversized source field.

tests.name: preview_expression sends one request per call and names the templates it rendered
tests.reason: Expression preview maps single/plural templates/default mode/pinned/run/node options to endpoint, labels independent renders by caller template and preserves source/available metadata; invalid counts/combinations and missing targets retain codes. Detects results attached to wrong expression.

tests.name: preview_expression fits large renders, values and outlines under the result cap
tests.reason: Large text/value renders clip explicitly, small render stays whole and wide available shape is simplified with omission flag under60k byte result cap. Detects unreadable oversized tool response or partial values misrepresented as complete.

tests.name: workflowUnion: the project, every projectOverride, a temp project's workspace and each sub-workflow's own (recursively); removed members are listed, not refused
tests.reason: Project union includes root, overrides, temporary workspace and recursive children; missing targets are reported, cycles stop. Literal known scope set catches hidden cross-project execution or recursion; cards consume this semantic security resolver, and card representative fixtures do not cover cyclic/temp/missing combinations.

tests.name: a chat create's scope is the union: another project makes the Admin card ungrantable even in Full access, and the card names each workspace's git identity
tests.reason: Chat create approval scope includes every union project/workspace git identity; any non-own project/temp target makes grant unavailable. Actual card fields catch consent omitting execution destination; external mapping and pure union do not protect grant/card use.

tests.name: a create card is complete: triggers, code and shell in full, the whole HTTP request, agent prompts in full incl. a saved prompt's body by title, the union, validation problems
tests.reason: Create approval must show complete executable code, shell/env, HTTP headers/body, agent prompts/accounts, saved prompt currentbody+append, execution union and validation warnings; denied card performs no create. Literal full data catches hidden dangerous instructions; definitions may contain 30k source, distinct from tool-result clipping. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: PREVIEW_TOO_LARGE: a change whose whole preview passes 1 MiB is refused before any card
tests.reason: Whole create preview over1MiB refuses PREVIEW_TOO_LARGE before opening card. Independent three400KiB source fixture catches authorizing unseen executable content; not covered by transport result60k cap.

tests.name: an update card shows the ops, the graph diff and the changed blocks in full (unchanged ones listed); enabling shows every block
tests.reason: Update card shows patch ops, graph additions, removed/added changed source and new block body, while unchanged bodies are summarized; enabling displays all newly armed blocks. Detects a user approving missing execution changes; no whole serialized hunk oracle is required. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: an update or create the daemon would refuse is refused before any card: a stale revision, a failing op, enabling with errors
tests.reason: Stale revision, invalid op or enabling an errorful definition must fail before any card/write. Literal invalid target/severity fixtures catch approval prompts for operations that cannot be honored; external dry-run does not protect chat approval ordering.

tests.name: delete and run cards: what is removed; the run's revision, enabled state and input
tests.reason: Delete card discloses active runs, all paginated recorded runs and ownsecret blast radius; run card pins revision/enabled/force and complete input, stale revision never cards. Detects consent hiding removed data or different run arguments. Approval assertions retain target names, global/project/provider/repository identity, meaningful values and security state; incidental title/scope wording is no longer frozen.

tests.name: PREVIEW_STALE: the workflow edited while its update or run card waited — nothing written, no run
tests.reason: Workflow revision changed while update/run approval waits must block write/start; a different frozen revision at actual start cancels the run; a native late patch conflict becomes PREVIEW_STALE. Deterministic changed revisions and no-write/cancel results catch consent TOCTOU beyond initial revision validation.

tests.name: PREVIEW_STALE: a saved prompt the card showed in full changed before the write
tests.reason: A saved prompt body shown in create approval is pinned; swapping that body after approval must block creation. Literal original/swapped body catches execution differing from approved instructions while workflow revision remains unchanged.

tests.name: set_workflow_secret from a chat: no value argument; the user types it into the card; it reaches the store and nowhere else; never grantable
tests.reason: Chat cannot supply a secret value; the user types it into a card and it flows only to the scoped store, never card/result. No grant is offered; global/delete scope is explicit and an older client returning no value writes nothing. Literal secret markers catch disclosure or bypass.

tests.name: chat reads claim the workflow's home: list_workflows defaults to the caller's project; another workspace's workflow cards below Full access
tests.reason: Chat listing defaults to its own project and refuses absent context; workflow metadata reads claim the stored home, requiring cross-workspace cards below Full access. Actual query/card family catches scope taken from the wrong context.

tests.name: cancel_workflow_run is Act in the project the run runs in: own project free, another workspace cards below Full access, a workflow-owned caller never acts away
tests.reason: Cancellation is Act at the run’s execution project: own project free, another workspace cards below Full, workflow-owned callers cannot act away and planning cannot cancel. Literal run paths and decisions catch borrowing the wrong definition scope or bypassing Act policy.

tests.name: workflow-owned callers get no Admin (ADMIN_NOT_AVAILABLE, no card); planning callers are refused Admin; dry runs stay available
tests.reason: Every Admin workflow tool rejects workflow-owned callers without a card and blocks planning; read-only dry runs remain available. The public family matrix catches an unguarded new mutation or denial of safe validation. Act cancellation follows a different rule.

tests.name: run_workflow fails closed after the start: an unreadable run is cancelled, a failed cancel is reported truthfully, the engine's refusal after a card is PREVIEW_STALE
tests.reason: An unreadable started run must be cancelled; failed cancellation must be reported truthfully with its id. Native late revision refusal maps to PREVIEW_STALE only after consent, otherwise REVISION_CONFLICT. Independent HTTP failures catch unchecked side effects and false cancellation reports.

tests.name: a run card shows the definition that will run in full, and pins every sub-workflow's revision (PREVIEW_STALE when one changes)
tests.reason: Run approval shows complete code and pins disabled child revision; a child edit during approval blocks start. Literal child revision/code catch unapproved child execution, while disabled children remain truthfully callable.

tests.name: run_workflow: the run's frozen sub-workflows must be the pinned revisions, else it is cancelled (PREVIEW_STALE)
tests.reason: A started run’s frozen child revision must match the pin or trigger cancellation/PREVIEW_STALE; matching revisions start and watch exposes that map. Literal frozen revisions catch the race between post-card check and engine freeze.

tests.name: grants fail closed on a union member that no longer resolves, and cover a sub-workflow only when the same grant covers it
tests.reason: A missing union project fails closed despite a parent grant; a child is covered only when the same grant covers parent and child. Literal grant membership and missing scope catch authority over unknown or ungranted execution; pure union only computes destinations.

tests.name: secrets: editing what a secret-reading block does is never granted (card every time); an unrelated edit stays covered
tests.reason: Retargeting a secret reader, changing its interpolated upstream input or adding a reader requires an ungrantable card despite an existing grant; unrelated edits remain covered. Actual card outcomes catch secret exfiltration through previously approved workflows; classifier syntax cases alone cannot protect gate use.

tests.name: reverse direction: a grant never covers changing or deleting a workflow that a workflow outside the grant runs as a sub-workflow (directly or through others); running it stays covered
tests.reason: Changing/deleting a callee requires approval when direct/transitive callers are outside its grant or unknown; running it remains covered, and a complete same-grant chain permits edits. Literal reference graphs catch indirect modification of user workflows; the real-port race case owns only the final precondition.

tests.name: changesSecretUse: added, changed, newly reachable and (for interpolating blocks) upstream changes count; unrelated ones do not
tests.reason: Retain semantic secret classification: reader edits, constant versus node-interpolated destinations, transitive upstream impact, plain prose and an unused standard destructuring signature. Remove the unused before argument and null-only branch. Literal source/templates expose credible credential-warning failures without asserting touched-set shape.

tests.name: an update card shows in full what the change makes run: an added edge's target and its downstream, newly reachable blocks, a re-routed if's branches
tests.reason: Connecting dormant executable work must reveal that target and downstream bodies; changing an if condition must reveal affected branches, excluding unrelated work. Actual card bodies catch consent hiding code made reachable without editing its source.

tests.name: a run card whose DEFINITION is too large to show: measured whole, an outline with a red warning, the prompts listed, the input whole — never grantable
tests.reason: An oversized existing run definition receives a danger-marked outline with every block identity and saved-prompt summary; no grant covers it, input stays whole, and a smaller complete definition may use its grant. Literal data catch hidden execution authority or confusing create rejection with existing-run outline policy.

tests.name: an input too large to show is PREVIEW_TOO_LARGE before any card (never cut, never outlined away)
tests.reason: Input over the preview cap is refused before card/start; it must never be truncated or hidden by an outlined definition. Literal 1.1MiB input catches unseen arguments reaching execution; oversized definitions intentionally allow a distinct outline path.

tests.name: a create records its children only on an explicit grant choice
tests.reason: Workflow children join a standing grant only on explicit grant selection. Actual recorded child sets and approval outcome are independent authority oracles, unlike removed warning-heading-only checks; executor generic grants do not know workflow child identity.

tests.name: a sub-workflow that does not exist makes the card ungrantable, even under a grant naming both
tests.reason: A nonexistent child makes its parent ungrantable even if the saved grant names both ids; a card remains required. Literal child404 catches stale membership authorizing an unknown definition; a missing project is a different scope failure.

tests.name: create_workflow's stale pins name the sub-workflow that changed
tests.reason: A child revision changed during create approval yields PREVIEW_STALE identifying that child and performs no create. Literal ids/revisions catch the create path forgetting executable dependency pins; run uses another side-effect path.

tests.name: workflowsReferencingPrompt (for Task 12): every workflow whose agent blocks use the saved prompt, with those blocks
tests.reason: Prompt references return every matching agent block under the right workflow, none for unused prompts, and unknown for relevant unreadable definitions/index failures. Literal graph and future records catch granting Act on a workflow-used prompt; saved-prompt gate representatives do not cover all resolver classifications.

tests.name: parent view: every kind, tools folded per toolUseId, subagent rows as anchors, ordered by time
tests.reason: Project an ordered mixed snapshot into public timeline entries: fold tool start/update/completion, preserve attachments, checkpoint totals, approval decisions, questions and plans; replace subagent bodies with anchors and roster. Literal expected data catch incorrect MCP projection; provider/UI tests do not assert this wire result.

tests.name: drill-in view shows only that agent's rows; reasoning and tools are opt-in
tests.reason: Drill-in returns only the requested agent and an empty roster; include options control reasoning, tools and activity while retaining core conversation. Literal owners and kinds catch cross-agent mixing or ignored filters; the parent projection does not test this selection.

tests.name: turns selects the last N turns; shedding drops reasoning, then tool detail, then the oldest turn
tests.reason: Last-N selection and shedding discard reasoning before tool detail and oldest turns, preserving a marked detail prefix. Literal turn/content fixtures catch off-by-one windows or losing important answers first. The focused reasoning test separately proves detail is untouched when its cut is unnecessary.

tests.name: an agent's anchor stamped with its own agentId stays in the parent view, a stamped background shell's does not; the roster decides title and status
tests.reason: A task anchor stamped with its own agentId remains in the parent, but a stamped background shell does not; current roster state overrides stale completion. Literal resumed status and owners catch missing anchors or duplicated agent work, distinct from ordinary unstamped anchors.

tests.name: a plan is actionable while it is the latest one and no later message implements it
tests.reason: Only the latest retained plan is actionable, then an implementation message clears it. Literal plan ids and expected true/false values catch an agent offering an obsolete implementation action; the historical-plan case protects a different host-window rule.

tests.name: an error or warning without a detail reads the payload's message, where runtime.error keeps its text
tests.reason: Runtime errors/warnings use the full payload message when detail is absent and the summary was clipped, without duplicating the warning. Literal complete cause catches hidden failure details; the general mixed fixture already has detail.

tests.name: a turn's opening message, written with the idle session's null turnId, is numbered through Turn.userMessageId
tests.reason: Opening users stored with null turnId map through Turn.userMessageId into the correct numbered turn and last-turn window. Two literal asks catch omitted or misnumbered prompts; already-stamped records cannot expose this association.

tests.name: a turn the host never started stays visible: alone, and before the first turn that did start
tests.reason: A failed turn the host never started remains visible before any started turn and before a retry, while counts/ranges stay accurate. Literal failure and user rows catch missing start refusals; successful turn binding requires a record that is absent here.

tests.name: maxChars is a hard budget: an oversized newest turn sheds its oldest rows and keeps its final reply
tests.reason: A busy newest turn sheds oldest rows while preserving final reply and newest tools; an oversized answer clips to a marked prefix under the whole-result budget. A literal final marker and independent JSON byte count catch lost answers or oversized results; escaped/Unicode cases exercise different byte costs.

tests.name: at maxChars 2 000 a final reply whose JSON outgrows its code points survives within the budget
tests.reason: JSON escaping counts toward the 2000-byte budget while the answer survives as a marked prefix. Literal quote/newline content catches budgeting source code points instead of serialized bytes; CJK input does not exercise escape expansion.

tests.name: maxChars counts UTF-8 bytes: a CJK reply is cut to what fits in bytes, never through a character
tests.reason: CJK and emoji answers clip on whole characters within 2000 JSON bytes. Independent Buffer encoding/round-trip and literal prefix catch byte/code-point confusion or split surrogates; ASCII escaping has another cost model.

tests.name: a roster over the budget is trimmed, oldest settled rows first, before any row of the latest turn
tests.reason: Roster overflow removes oldest settled agents before the newest turn, keeps the newest settled suffix and sets truncation flags. Independent ids plus whole user/reply data catch fleets swallowing conversation; all-live fallback has another priority.

tests.name: 100 long-titled subagents at 55 000: titles capped at 200 code points, every live row kept, the oldest settled ones dropped
tests.reason: A hundred long multibyte titles at 55k retain marked 200-code-point titles, every running agent and the newest settled subset. Literal title sizes, running id set and encoded byte bound catch title overflow or dropped running work; short rosters cannot trigger this.

tests.name: a result at exactly maxChars bytes remains whole; one byte less requires truncation
tests.reason: At the exact independent public-response JSON size, return the entire expected response; at one byte less, report bounded truncation. The expected schema/data are built independently, catching off-by-one or unconditional shedding.

tests.name: 30 running agents beside one short turn: the user row and the reply come back whole, the roster takes the rest
tests.reason: If all thirty agents are running, preserve the user and answer and trim oldest live roster rows with a flag. Literal newest-id order catches a missing all-live fallback or content starvation; settled-agent tests never enter this branch.

tests.name: coveredTurns names only turns with rows present: null when the window shows none
tests.reason: An agent with no rows in the requested last turn yields an empty list and coveredTurns:null while total turnCount stays two. Literal empty range catches claiming turns with no delivered rows; populated pagination cannot.

tests.name: a latest turn whose newest row is a tool call with a 16 KB command: that row stays, its command cut to fit
tests.reason: An oversized newest command keeps the meaningful running tool row and marked command prefix/title. Literal command data and byte bound catch discarding running work when no whole string fits; answer-protection tests have a different spared row.

tests.name: a running turn whose newest row is a 60-file patch: that row stays, its file list capped to a head and a count of the rest
tests.reason: An oversized newest file patch keeps its row, original path prefix and omitted count instead of an empty result. Independent paths and counts catch list-valued fields not being reducible; command strings do not exercise list summaries.

tests.name: a turn whose newest row is a 1 500-file checkpoint: that row stays, its files capped, the rest counted with their line totals
tests.reason: A 1500-file checkpoint keeps a prefix plus omitted file count and addition/deletion totals with a whole modest roster. Totals computed from independent fixture files catch losing change volume; ordinary changed-file lists lack line counts.

tests.name: dropping an oversized prompt leaves room for all live agents and the newest settled agents
tests.reason: Dropping a 30k prompt reclaims space for every live agent and newer settled agents. Literal running ids and settled suffix catch a fixed roster allocation wasting room; roster-only trimming does not require redistributing freed prompt space.

tests.name: reasoning goes before tool detail: when dropping it is enough, every tool keeps its whole detail
tests.reason: When removing reasoning alone resolves overflow, retain the complete tool detail. Literal 1500-character output and absent reasoning catch eager second-stage clipping; the general priority fixture needs both stages and cannot expose this unnecessary cut.

tests.name: the spared row is the latest turn's reply, not a newer row after it: a budget for one row keeps the reply
tests.reason: The latest turn answer outranks a later checkpoint when only one row fits. Literal answer text catches sparing the last chronological row; ordinary examples place the answer last.

tests.name: beforeTurn reads the turns just before it; olderTurns counts the started turns before the range
tests.reason: beforeTurn excludes its anchor, olderTurns counts started turns before the delivered range, count+1 reads latest, and the earliest range reports zero older. Literal third/fourth messages catch cursor skips or repeats; last-N alone has no backwards anchor.

tests.name: a row with no turn belongs to the range by its time: from the first turn's request (from the very start at turn 1), before the next turn's
tests.reason: Turnless failure rows follow [request,next request) time intervals, including prehistory at turn one and the exact next-request boundary. Literal labels/timestamps catch missing or duplicated historical failures; opening-user association uses an explicit message id.

tests.name: a historical call start and retained completion project as one entry at the start time in its latest state
tests.reason: A historical start merged with a retained completion becomes one tool at its start time in its latest state, preserving command/output. Literal row data catch duplicate tools, wrong ordering or stale running state during pagination.

tests.name: the actionable plan is judged on the window: a plan only a page holds has aged out, and is not the one implement_plan would send
tests.reason: A plan found only on an older page is not actionable if it aged out of the host window; the same plan retained in that window is actionable. Literal window selection catches confusing readable history with the actual implement_plan target.

tests.name: unavailable turns reserve room for their hint at the whole-result byte boundary
tests.reason: Unavailable-turn hint bytes are reserved at the exact whole-result boundary, the range is reported, and overflow truncates appropriately. An independently built response and literal hint byte size catch a final envelope cap dropping otherwise valid entries.

tests.name: a Grok-shaped command whose detail repeats the command shows its output, and an echo with no output never clears it
tests.reason: A Grok command echo is not output; a real partial output survives an echo-only completion. Literal captured protocol shape and partial marker catch bogus output or erased output; generic command records have another provider layout.

tests.name: outputItemId names the call's completion when the read cut it — the row the GUI's "Load full output" reads
tests.reason: A cut completion exposes its own item id for read_tool_output; an uncut completion with no extra output exposes none. Independent completion id and first-line preview catch an unusable Load full output link.

tests.name: without streamed output, outputItemId is never an update: ingestion stores it already cut, so its item holds nothing the row does not
tests.reason: An update already stored slimmed must not advertise more output, even after an empty completion; a whole cut completion may. Literal row ids and data catch linking to the same preview or hiding the real completion behind a stale update.

tests.name: without streamed output, outputItemId is never a call's start, where the read cut its input, not its output; a denial the read cut is offered
tests.reason: A cut start contains input, so offers no full output; a cut denial can expose its full detail. Independent start/denial ids catch treating any truncated payload as output; normal completions do carry output.

tests.name: a call that streamed output offers its latest row as outputItemId, where no completion was cut
tests.reason: Command chunks make the latest start/update/completion id readable even if payload was not cut; another call’s chunks do not, and chunks are not independent timeline rows. Literal call/row ids catch missing full-stream access or misattributed output.

tests.name: a background shell's row, in its own drill-in, offers outputItemId — its chunks count wherever its turn range ends
tests.reason: Background-shell drill-in recognizes output arriving in the next turn outside the queried range, gives the right row id/status and keeps owned work out of the parent. Literal two-turn fixtures catch losing output when the launch turn ends.

tests.name: only a command's streamed output counts: a file change streaming its result's text offers nothing more
tests.reason: file_change_output does not create readable command output; command_output does. Literal stream kinds catch Edit/Write success text incorrectly exposed through terminal-output APIs.

tests.name: in a drill-in, a command whose rows retention dropped is an entry built from its latest chunk in the range
tests.reason: If retention dropped all call rows, drill-in reconstructs one tool from the latest command chunk in the selected range, using its id; tools opt-out and file-change chunks yield none. Literal ids/turns catch disappearing background work or duplicating each chunk.

tests.name: a background task's chunk-built entry is titled from its roster row; a subagent's roster row names none of its calls
tests.reason: A chunk-only background title uses a real background roster description, never an agent description or placeholder id; actual call title outranks roster, which outranks command fallback. Independent names catch misleading command identity.

tests.name: a chunk-built entry takes the call's title, command and end from its rows in the view, outside the range
tests.reason: A chunk in the selected range borrows command/title/final state from call rows outside that range, while its id still reads range output. A literal failed later completion catches false running status or lost context; pure chunk fixtures have no outside context.

tests.name: in a drill-in, a subagent's command with a streamed chunk offers its completion as outputItemId
tests.reason: A stamped subagent command chunk belongs to its drill-in and exposes the completion id. Literal agent and row ids catch streams ignored for nested calls; ownerless parent commands cannot.

tests.name: an older log's UNSTAMPED chunk of a subagent's call is that subagent's: its drill-in offers the completion
tests.reason: A legacy unstamped chunk inherits its call’s agent owner; another agent’s drill-in remains empty. Captured Claude legacy shape catches compatibility loss or misattribution; stamped chunks require no inference.

tests.name: the parent view builds no entry from a chunk alone, stamped or not
tests.reason: The parent never synthesizes tools from subagent chunks alone, stamped or not, even when owner rows aged out. Literal absence catches nested work leaking into the parent; drill-in recovery intentionally synthesizes a row.

tests.name: a call whose rows are all turnless, ownerless and unclosed is no entry — what a rewind of the turn they preceded left
tests.reason: Legacy rewind leftovers that are turnless, ownerless and unclosed yield no ghost tool; adopted, closed and owned calls remain visible. Independent old persisted shapes catch phantom running work without discarding real subagent/background calls. Durable old logs keep this compatibility relevant.

tests.name: hooks: a failed completion is an error row, a cancelled one a warning row; starts, progress and successes are no row
tests.reason: Failed hook completion is an error, cancellation a warning; bookkeeping/success are hidden and activity opt-in applies. Literal outcomes catch lost hook failures or noisy progress; generic runtime errors have different semantics.

tests.name: a commentary message is an assistant row marked commentary: true; the turn's answer carries no such field
tests.reason: Commentary carries commentary:true while answer and legacy assistant rows omit the field. Literal messageKind records catch narration misclassified as an answer and incorrect public field presence; the budget test chooses a row but does not verify all forms.

tests.name: the spared commentary is the latest turn's LAST: an earlier one, a newer tool row and an older turn's answer all go before it
tests.reason: Surviving owner: without an answer, spare the latest turn’s LAST commentary over older narration, newer tools and an older turn’s answer; clip a marked prefix. Once an answer arrives, it takes priority. Distinct literal markers catch choosing the wrong turn or stale commentary.

tests.name: compaction rows follow the shared rule: no state is settled, the legacy marker counts, a subagent's own stays out of the parent view
tests.reason: Legacy missing-state compaction, old spelling and staged states project correctly; unrelated state is excluded, subagent compaction stays out of the parent and activity opt-in applies. Literal states/tokens catch compatibility loss or wrong context boundaries.

tests.name: goal rows read as the GUI's timeline shows them: each change a line of its own, labelled by its summary, in log order; the progress tick is none
tests.reason: Goal changes and status requests each produce their own ordered info row with supplied summary; progress heartbeat is hidden and activity opt-in applies. Literal protocol summaries are passed data, not text generated by the tested code, catching missing history or duplicate heartbeat.

tests.name: a goal that can't be met and a failed /goal command are error rows with the GUI's text; a goal row the GUI cannot read is still a line of its own
tests.reason: Failed goal/command are errors with cause; future unknown changes and malformed progress remain generic info rows. Literal unknown schema/cause catch forward-compatible events being silently dropped; ordinary goal changes parse cleanly.

tests.name: the parent view of a Claude thread has no row for a re-emitted opening paragraph: the first occurrence stays where it was said
tests.reason: Claude parent drops a legacy re-emitted opening copy while preserving the original position and actual answer; tight budgets spare that answer. Distinct literal opening/answer markers catch an old duplicate becoming last reply. Durable old logs preserve this regression risk.

tests.name: a drill-in and a Codex thread keep every message: only a Claude thread's parent view drops a copy, as in the GUI
tests.reason: The same repeated words in Codex or an agent drill-in remain visible; only Claude parent history has the documented duplicate artifact. Literal adapter/agent contexts catch broad deduplication deleting real messages; positive Claude examples cannot.

tests.name: a read with older pages merged under the window counts the copies over all of it: the opening a page brought back finds the copy
tests.reason: Merging a history page containing the opening detects the later duplicate; a mid-turn window alone retains the available distinct messages. Literal full/window fixtures catch deduplication consulting only the retained window after history retrieval.

tests.name: a workflow run is one coordinator anchor in the parent view and excludes member-owned rows
tests.reason: Workflow member launches, completions and owned work fold into one coordinator anchor with real title/status. Literal group/member ids catch a fleet flooding parent history or leaking member bodies; direct subagents have no grouping.

tests.name: members whose roster rows aged out still fold into their coordinator's anchor, by the id before their slot
tests.reason: If member roster records age out, stable slot ids still fold them into the coordinator. An empty roster and literal group id catch duplicate anchors after cache retention; a complete roster cannot.

tests.name: a 100-agent workflow over the budget sheds its members, never its coordinator or the direct subagents
tests.reason: Over-budget hundred-member workflow drops settled members before its coordinator/direct agents, keeps live members and retains total progress. Literal ids/counts plus byte cap catch losing navigation or misreporting fleet state; flat rosters have no coordinator priority.

tests.name: usageView preserves scoped percentages, reset instants, freshness and account auth state
tests.reason: Quota projection must preserve literal percentages/reset instants/freshness/account auth state, distinguish system/aggregate records and avoid duplicate family windows when accounts exist.

tests.name: session views distinguish a new chat from running and exited terminals
tests.reason: New idle chat reason differs from running terminal null and exited terminal reason; fixed reason values protect caller wait/attention meaning.

tests.name: sessionView projects a chat summary and a terminal summary
tests.reason: Public view mapping must distinguish chat vs terminal fields, account/system identity, Global/profile refs and project decomposition; protocol field placement is stable, not markup.

tests.name: sessionDetail merges the head, context window, pending requests, plan, roster and last reply
tests.reason: Session detail must merge head options/account/supports/pending request semantics/context25%/plan/roster and latest main reply, excluding subagent text. This owns positive helper-to-detail wiring.

tests.name: pending views: advertised decisions win over the default four; a message-mode question is dismissible
tests.reason: Advertised decisions and warnings override defaults, empty options restore four, message question remains dismissible/multiselect; provider choice contract differs from command response mapping.

tests.name: pending views: an approval's reason is shown when the provider gave one
tests.reason: Provider approval reason must survive view construction and remain absent when none supplied; data explanation may be security-relevant, unlike exact application copy.

tests.name: buildViewContext reads registry, accounts and providers and tolerates a failing providers call
tests.reason: Failed providers read must not break registry/account identity mapping; supports fail closed while valid agent/account data remains usable.

tests.name: the context meter skips a row without a usable reading, as the host's snapshot drop rule expects
tests.reason: Malformed latest context row must be skipped for earlier valid50k/200k reading, and null-only yields absent; otherwise slimmed/incomplete rows blank meter.

tests.name: planView reports a plan the snapshot's wire slimming already cut as truncated
tests.reason: Already-wire-truncated plan must retain truncated=true even when its short visible text fits local cap; local length alone cannot recover upstream data loss marker.

tests.name: the context meter's percentUsed is clamped to 100, as the GUI's ring is; the raw token counts are kept
tests.reason: Over-window250k/200k must preserve raw counts and cap percent100; exact200k boundary remains100. UI numeric formatting isn't under test, public data is.

tests.name: lastReply is the turn's answer: Codex commentary (the fold's messageKind) is left out while the turn has an answer
tests.reason: When final answer exists, commentary must not join lastReply; unphased older-provider messages still join. Retained API last-reply test does not include messageKind phase classification.

tests.name: a turn with no answer at all ends on its last commentary, as the GUI's timeline does; a subagent's commentary never counts
tests.reason: Without final answer, last main commentary alone must answer interrupted turn, excluding child text; an actual answer wins even with later narration. Distinct fallback from phased answer owner.

tests.name: plan.actionable is judged on the snapshot with the host's own rule, never on the summary flag one poll behind
tests.reason: Fresh snapshot plan actionability beats stale summary both directions, preventing get_session telling callers to implement an already-sent plan.

tests.name: a subagent's title, progress and error are capped at 200 code points in a session view, a cut ending in "…"
tests.reason: Subagent title/progress/error must cap200 code points without broken emoji and leave short fields whole; tests concrete transport preview bounds, not visual geometry.

tests.name: a session detail keeps within the result cap: 100 long subagents beside a 16 KB plan and reply shed settled rows oldest first, then live ones; every other field stays whole
tests.reason: Over-cap roster must shed oldest settled before live, then oldest live only when necessary, preserving plan/reply/request; ordered results fit60000 and flags expose loss.

tests.name: a plan and a reply of 16 384 wide characters pass the cap on their own: the reply is cut by bytes first, then the plan, on code-point boundaries, each marked truncated; every other field stays whole
tests.reason: Multibyte reply/plan must be cut by bytes in priority order with correct flags and code-point boundaries, preserve other data and keep fitting small text whole.

tests.name: chat.goal is the summary's unfinished goal, its objective cut to 200 code points ending in "…"; a session without one reads null
tests.reason: Summary goal must keep unfinished active status while bounding objective200 code points; absent/null goal is Global-style null, not phantom goal.

tests.name: chat.goal tells a goal that stopped short from a finished session, which reason alone cannot: every settled turn reads "completed"
tests.reason: Paused/blocked/budget/usage-limited unfinished goals must remain visible despite completed turn reason; dropping them would falsely imply task completion to MCP callers.

tests.name: chat.goal reads the summary defensively, as the GUI's tab marker does: a finished goal, or one without a usable objective or status, is null
tests.reason: Finished/malformed goals must disappear and continuing requires booleantrue; boundary parsing prevents malformed old-daemon summaries claiming live work.

tests.name: goal-continuing: between two turns of a goal the provider continues by itself, a settled turn reads working — the ladder's own rung — with no finished stamp
tests.reason: Active goal continuing between turns must remain working with no finished attention stamp despite completed last turn; ordinary settled session is completed.

tests.name: the detail's goal is the fold's, a finished one too while the provider's last update carries it, with every fact the provider reported and nothing else; list_sessions shows only an unfinished one
tests.reason: Detail must retain finished goal counters/facts while summary list omits completed goal; provider internal goalId must not be exposed as public identity.

tests.name: the detail's goal is continuing on the summary's word, and get_session's supports carry the provider's goal surface
tests.reason: Detail continuing derives from summary authorization and exposes provider goal actions/facts including explicit null budget, not invented absent counters.

tests.name: a stale summary's continuing never outlives the snapshot's goal: only an active goal continues, as the host's own predicate has it
tests.reason: Snapshot paused/blocked/limited/complete/failed goal must override stale active-continuing summary; otherwise MCP says autonomous work continues after it stopped.

tests.name: goals §5.7: a goal an Orquester update holds reads paused, continuing and heldForUpdate — in a list and in a detail, the GUI's "paused for update"
tests.reason: Deploy-held paused goal is working/continuing/heldForUpdate in list/detail; resumed active clears hold, terminal states stop, and user pause is never inferred a deploy hold.

tests.name: the detail's cleared or missing goal overrides a stale continuing summary
tests.reason: Cleared/missing snapshot goal must override stale continuing summary and return null; older host compatibility cannot resurrect a deleted goal.

tests.name: the detail's goal text is cut in code points, ending in "…": an objective at 4 000, a last check at 2 000, a phase at 200; an objective at the limit stays whole
tests.reason: Goal objective4000/check2000/phase200 caps must preserve code points and exact-limit objectivewhole; fields are independently documented MCP preview contracts.

tests.name: a goal at its caps stays whole beside a 16 KB plan and reply and a large request: fitDetail cuts the reply, then the plan, to make room, never the goal
tests.reason: Maximal goal facts and pending request must remain whole under60000 pressure while reply then plan shed; ordinary text-only fitting cannot protect reserved goal data.

tests.name: a workflow run lists its coordinator with the run's progress, then its members by phase and slot; no host path is shown
tests.reason: Workflow coordinator/member grouping, phase-slot ordering, retry count/result/error/usage must map correctly with no host script/transcript path leakage; individual subagents don't protect workflow privacy/identity.

tests.name: a subagent's result is a bounded preview, cut like its other text
tests.reason: Subagent result has its own capped200-character field, flagging cut with ellipsis; title/progress/error cap tests cannot catch result accidentally omitted or stored whole.

tests.name: waitForTurn: a new turn completing after the baseline, a pending question, a plan, an error, and a steer
tests.reason: A turn wait must distinguish a new completion, needs-input, actionable plan, failure and completion of a steered running turn.

tests.name: waitForTurn: an error the session showed before the message (a failed CLI start) is not this message's outcome
tests.reason: A pre-existing CLI-start failure must not be mistaken for the newly posted message outcome; a new failed-start stamp must settle correctly.

tests.name: waitForTurn: the baseline turn itself never counts, a timeout reports timeout, a closed session throws
tests.reason: A baseline completed turn must not satisfy a new wait; timeout and closure must return their distinct public outcomes.

tests.name: waitForAttention: cursor semantics, immediate return, settle window collects siblings, timeout
tests.reason: Attention cursors must return only later instants, retain the greatest stamp and collect same-poll siblings during the documented settle window.

tests.name: waitForTurn: every event is evaluated, so a completion followed at once by the next turn is still reported
tests.reason: A completion immediately followed by another running turn must remain observable, rather than being overwritten by latest state.

tests.name: waitForTurn: a plan-ready baseline (implement_plan) does not count until the latest turn moves past it
tests.reason: A pre-existing actionable plan cannot complete the implement-plan message wait until the turn moves.

tests.name: an exited terminal keeps its finished attention through summaries that omit activity (a rename, the settle re-read)
tests.reason: Exited terminal attention must survive later summaries omitting activity, preventing missed finished tabs.

tests.name: aborting an attention wait during settling releases the subscription; cursor offsets denote instants
tests.reason: Abort during settling must unsubscribe, and equivalent timezone-offset timestamps must compare as instants.

tests.name: a late session.exited cannot bring a closed tab back into the watch
tests.reason: An exit event after closure must not resurrect the closed session or advance its attention cursor.

tests.name: activity published during the initial list read is preserved, with the newest stamp winning
tests.reason: Activity events arriving during initial listing must remain merged with the newest recorded stamp for each session.

tests.name: a sibling stamped while the settle window's re-read is in flight is still collected
tests.reason: A sibling becoming ready during settle reread must be collected before the shared cursor advances past it.

tests.name: a single-session wait ends with SESSION_NOT_FOUND when its session closes, or is already gone at the first read
tests.reason: A selected session missing initially or closing during wait must fail SESSION_NOT_FOUND and remove listeners.

tests.name: a project-wide or unfiltered attention wait just stops watching a closed session
tests.reason: Broad/project watches must drop closed sessions while continuing to return remaining matching sessions.

tests.name: a single-session attention wait is scoped by its sessionId alone, so no selection can disagree with it
tests.reason: Single-session watches must select only the explicit sessionId, independent of unrelated selection predicates.

tests.name: waitForTurn: while the host reports a goal continuing, a new settled turn is a pause between two goal turns — the wait goes on until the goal stops
tests.reason: Goal-continuation gaps between settled turns must not end the wait; an actual pause or pending question must.

tests.name: waitForTurn: an errored session whose goal the host still reports continuing (a restart's owed resume) is not failed until the goal stops continuing
tests.reason: A goal resume owed across restart must hold an old error until continuing:false confirms actual failure.

tests.name: waitWhileWorking re-reads each chat's HEAD on every bus event, never its whole snapshot
tests.reason: Bus wakes must refresh slim head state until the real reply settles, returning correct lastTurn/reply without fetching whole snapshots.
